## Summary

Remove the Java authoring DSL (`pathland-view`) entirely and make **Kotlin the only JVM authoring DSL** before 1.0.

The JVM engine/runtime (`pathland-view-core`) stays; the Kotlin DSL (`pathland-view-kotlin`) becomes the sole supported way to author JVM views. Java is no longer an authoring target, though it remains an implementation/host language where needed.

## Motivation

- One JVM authoring surface instead of two.
- Stop maintaining duplicate Java/Kotlin view and modifier surfaces.
- Avoid Java/Kotlin API drift and repeated parity work.
- Align the JVM story with the Kotlin-first direction.
- Remove Java-only build machinery (`State` annotation processor, Java constructor-enforcement processor).
- Make future work (including a possible KMP spike) easier by having one JVM DSL.

## Current state

- Java DSL: `lib/java/pathland-view` — 101 files, ~8.1k LOC, ~4.6k lines of tests.
- Java-only processor: `lib/java/pathland-view-processor` (`State` binding + authoring-convention checks).
- Kotlin DSL: `lib/java/pathland-view-kotlin` — Kotlin-owned views/modifiers over `pathland-view-core`, currently JVM-only.
- Java DSL is used by:
  - `pathland-demo-views` (36 files, ~2.7k LOC)
  - `pathland-gtk-demo`
  - `pathland-qt-demo`
  - `pathland-quarkus-demo`
  - `pathland-spring-boot-demo`
  - Java tests in `pathland-server-core`, `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-quarkus`, and `pathland-spring-boot-starter`
  - `pathland-spring-boot-starter` production dependency
  - `pathland-quarkus-java` + `pathland-quarkus-starter`
- Kotlin parity tests currently use the Java DSL as a test-scope oracle.
- `spec/DSL.md`, `README.md`, and `AGENTS.md` are still Java-centric.

## Decisions

state.output:
- Java authoring is a non-goal.
- Kotlin is the only JVM authoring DSL.
- Removal happens before 1.0; breaking changes are acceptable.
- Java GTK and Qt demos will be ported to Kotlin, not dropped.
- The Java core API is not necessarily public. Keep `pathland-view-core` as needed for the engine/SPI, but document it as an implementation/SPI surface, not an authoring API.
- Keep the artifact name `pathland-view-kotlin`; do not reuse the old `pathland-view` name for Kotlin.
- Kotlin Multiplatform support is explicitly out of scope for this issue.

## Scope

### Remove

- [ ] `lib/java/pathland-view`
- [ ] `lib/java/pathland-view-processor`
- [ ] `pathland-quarkus-java`
- [ ] `pathland-quarkus-java-deployment`
- [ ] `pathland-quarkus-starter` compatibility alias
- [ ] Java Quarkus demo (`pathland-quarkus-demo`) once the Kotlin demo covers it
- [ ] Java DSL test-scope dependencies everywhere
- [ ] Java DSL release artifacts and documentation references

### Keep

- [ ] `pathland-view-core` as the JVM engine/SPI
- [ ] `pathland-view-kotlin` as the sole JVM authoring DSL
- [ ] `pathland-quarkus` (DSL-neutral) and `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`
- [ ] `pathland-server-core`, renderers, state, test kit

### Port to Kotlin

- [ ] `pathland-demo-views` (use `KotlinView` + `state()`)
- [ ] `pathland-gtk-demo` host code
- [ ] `pathland-qt-demo` host code
- [ ] `pathland-spring-boot-demo`
- [ ] Java test fixtures in `pathland-server-core`, `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-quarkus`, and `pathland-spring-boot-starter`
- [ ] Rename/update Java-specific demo run scripts

## Migration plan

### Phase 0 — Land the current in-flight refactors

- JVM engine split + Kotlin ownership.
- Quarkus core/Java/Kotlin extension split + Kotlin demo.
- These are transitional; the Java Quarkus extension and starter alias are deleted in Phase 3.

### Phase 1 — Make Kotlin independently conformant

- [ ] Move engine/runtime tests from `pathland-view` into `pathland-view-core`.
- [ ] Move DSL-level tests into `pathland-view-kotlin` and rewrite them in Kotlin.
- [ ] Replace Java-vs-Kotlin parity tests with Kotlin-only golden frame assertions.
- [ ] Run the shared engine traces through Kotlin.
- [ ] Cover every primitive, modifier, control, navigation path, media path, and `ViewThatFits`.
- [ ] Remove `pathland-view-kotlin`'s test-scope dependency on `pathland-view`.

Acceptance: Kotlin tests no longer need the Java DSL for confidence.

### Phase 2 — Port JVM demos to Kotlin

- [ ] Rewrite `pathland-demo-views` in Kotlin.
- [ ] Port GTK host to Kotlin; update run script.
- [ ] Port Qt host to Kotlin; update run script.
- [ ] Port Spring Boot demo to Kotlin.
- [ ] Delete the Java Quarkus demo; keep `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo`.
- [ ] Optionally have the Kotlin Quarkus demo mount the ported shared `MusicPlayerView`.

Acceptance: every surviving demo builds and runs without `pathland-view`.

### Phase 3 — Remove Java DSL and Java integrations

- [ ] Remove `pathland-view` and `pathland-view-processor` modules.
- [ ] Remove `pathland-quarkus-java`, its deployment module, and the starter alias.
- [ ] Make `pathland-spring-boot-starter` DSL-neutral.
- [ ] Remove Java DSL test dependencies from all modules.
- [ ] Add an Enforcer ban for `dev.pathland:pathland-view`.
- [ ] Remove Java DSL artifacts from the release workflow.

### Phase 4 — Docs/spec/status

- [ ] Rewrite `spec/DSL.md` around Kotlin; remove Java realization tables/sections.
- [ ] Update `README.md` examples and demo table.
- [ ] Update `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `RELEASING.md`.
- [ ] Update/delete affected `status.md` files.
- [ ] Add a migration note for Java users.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mvn -q -B test` passes.
- [ ] No production or test dependency on `dev.pathland:pathland-view`.
- [ ] `pathland-view`, `pathland-view-processor`, `pathland-quarkus-java`, and `pathland-quarkus-starter` no longer exist.
- [ ] Kotlin Quarkus demo, Spring Boot demo, GTK demo, and Qt demo all run on Kotlin-authored views.
- [ ] Release workflow publishes only the surviving JVM libraries.
- [ ] Docs/spec no longer present Java as the JVM reference realization.
- [ ] Existing Rust `pathland-view` crate is untouched.

## Risks / notes

- Kotlin's current test suite is much smaller than the Java DSL's; Phase 1 is mandatory before deletion.
- Spring Boot's Kotlin/compiler version must be aligned and tested.
- Root Kotlin is currently 2.2.20 while the Quarkus Kotlin extension/demo use 2.4.10; settle one version matrix before the port.
- Do not cut a release between the transitional Quarkus work and the removal if the transitional Java extension should not be published.
- Need to decide whether the Spring Boot starter remains core-only or gets a Kotlin convenience starter.

## Open questions

- Keep `pathland-view-kotlin` as the permanent artifact name? (Recommended: yes.)
- Should the Spring Boot starter stay core-only, with apps adding `pathland-view-kotlin`, or should there be a `pathland-spring-boot-kotlin` convenience artifact?
- Is `pathland-view-core` documented as public SPI or internal implementation detail?
- Which Kotlin version becomes the project-wide baseline?

## References

- `lib/java/pathland-view/`
- `lib/java/pathland-view-processor/`
- `lib/java/pathland-view-kotlin/`
- `lib/java/pathland-demo-views/`
- `lib/java/pathland-gtk-demo/`, `lib/java/pathland-qt-demo/`
- `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-java/`, `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-starter/`
- `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/`
- `spec/DSL.md`

        (dev.pathland.view.core.protocol), retained-tree diff emitter
        (dev.pathland.view.engine), Angular-style signals, wire codec, router, state, and
        lazy JNA ring interop. Shared by the Java and Kotlin authoring DSLs and by server
        runtimes. Runs on every LTS from Java 17; JNA is the only runtime dependency.
    </description>

            <groupId>net.java.dev.jna</groupId>

        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <!-- Point the test JVM at the Rust cdylib for JNA ring tests.
                         Absent the dylib, those tests are skipped via an assumption. -->
                    <argLine>-Djava.library.path=${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug</argLine>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

# pathland-demo-views-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

Kotlin-owned demo views over `pathland-view-kotlin`, with no Java-DSL dependency.
The first (and currently only) view is the app-driven music player.

## Implemented

- **`MusicPlayerView`** — Apple Music-style root: one root `SizeThatFits`
  selects narrow (no volume), medium (volume), or wide (volume + `NowPlayingSidebar`),
  with the floating `PlayerBar`.
- **Persisted player state** — `player.position`, `player.playing`,
  `player.track`, `player.volume`, `player.seekRequest`, `player.volumeRequest`
  via Kotlin `KotlinView` state delegates.
- **App-driven media** — a `MediaController` owns the source/transport; every
  fit candidate shares the same controller. `MEDIA_*` reports feed position/volume
  and `MEDIA_ENDED` advances the track.
- **Seek/volume decoupling** — `SeekControl` buffers drags and commits on release;
  `PercentSeek` maps seconds to 0..100; `VolumeControl` separates report from
  command.
- **Lyrics** — synchronized two-line karaoke pill driven by the parsed SRT cues.
- **Window metadata** — track-derived title/description and `locale("en")`.
- **Sponsored proxy** — optional `adUrl` appends a `ProxyView` in the sidebar.
- **Accessibility** — transport labels, slider labels, `MAIN`/`HEADER` roles.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Remaining demo views (KitchenSink, SplitNav, AdView) are still Java; tracked by
  #169.

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views-kotlin` — `LyricsTest`, `SeekControlTest`,
`MusicPlayerViewTest` (tree/render, fit swaps, media state, seek echo guard,
snapshot emission, sponsored proxy).
--- view-kotlin status ---
# pathland-view-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

The idiomatic Kotlin authoring surface (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`). Phase 3 is
complete: every production view/modifier is Kotlin-owned over
`pathland-view-core`; the Java DSL is a test-scope parity oracle only.

## Phase 3

- **Core-owned in Kotlin**: all primitives, shapes, stacks, grids, scroll/lazy
  containers, `ForEach`, `Button`, text/value controls, media, navigation,
  `Label`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`, `ProxyView`, and the complete modifier
  vocabulary (padding/frame/fonts/colors/borders/shadows/effects/transforms/
  interaction/accessibility/environment/styles/window metadata).
- **Dependency boundary**: main depends on `pathland-view-core` only; the Java
  DSL is test-scope for byte-for-byte parity comparisons.
- Tests compare the Kotlin-owned views and modifiers against the Java DSL.

## Implemented

- **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`, `Rectangle`,
  `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`, `Divider`, `Spacer`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
- **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
  `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
  `ProxyView`.
- **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
  `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
  `ColorPicker`.
- **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
  `.children(...)`. A custom `KotlinView` constructed inline in a block
  auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`
  inside `body()` (it does not leak into the enclosing scope). An explicit
  `view.add()` / `+view` is available for Java-constructed views (e.g.
  `mediaController.attach()`).
- **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
  `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`, `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
- **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
  layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
  foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
  visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
  environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents. A child
  modifier replaces its auto-registered leaf in the enclosing builder, so
  `VStack { Text("x").fontSize(20f) }` keeps the modifier. The Java
  `.modifiers(...)` operation remains available as an escape hatch.

# pathland-demo-views-kotlin — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

Kotlin-owned demo views over `pathland-view-kotlin`, with no Java-DSL dependency.
The first (and currently only) view is the app-driven music player.

## Implemented

- **`MusicPlayerView`** — Apple Music-style root: one root `SizeThatFits`
  selects narrow (no volume), medium (volume), or wide (volume + `NowPlayingSidebar`),
  with the floating `PlayerBar`.
- **Persisted player state** — `player.position`, `player.playing`,
  `player.track`, `player.volume`, `player.seekRequest`, `player.volumeRequest`
  via Kotlin `KotlinView` state delegates.
- **App-driven media** — a `MediaController` owns the source/transport; every
  fit candidate shares the same controller. `MEDIA_*` reports feed position/volume
  and `MEDIA_ENDED` advances the track.
- **Seek/volume decoupling** — `SeekControl` buffers drags and commits on release;
  `PercentSeek` maps seconds to 0..100; `VolumeControl` separates report from
  command.
- **Lyrics** — synchronized two-line karaoke pill driven by the parsed SRT cues.
- **Window metadata** — track-derived title/description and `locale("en")`.
- **Sponsored proxy** — optional `adUrl` appends a `ProxyView` in the sidebar.

- Remaining demo views (KitchenSink, SplitNav, AdView) are still Java; tracked by

parts.text:
Now, understand what "core view classes should be moved to kotlin as well" could mean in terms of effort and architecture. Let's check current `pathland-view-core` package composition:
- `dev.pathland.view.core` (54 root files, includes View/Environment/Color/Theme/etc. plus view wrappers EnvironmentView, TapGestureView, ReactiveSlotView, Modified, ViewBuilder...)
- subpackages protocol (9), router (11), signal (14), state (5), transport (6), ffm (2) = 47
- engine (8)

"core view classes" likely the root `dev.pathland.view.core` classes — the view vocabulary/SPI, not protocol/signal/state/transport/router/engine. Converting those ~54 to Kotlin would make the "core view classes" Kotlin. But Java server core and renderer use these classes from Java; Kotlin interop fine, but Java callers must still compile. Potential issues: Java static methods -> Kotlin companion/@JvmStatic, constants -> @JvmField, `View.modifiers` default method -> Kotlin interface with default impl (Java sees default method), etc.

Alternatively "core view classes" refers to the Java DSL's classes in `dev.pathland.view` (VStack, Text, etc.) — but those are removed. Hmm, user says "remove all java dsl, and core view classes should be moved to kotlin as well." Could mean "the core view classes [in pathland-view-core] should be moved to Kotlin as well". That's most literal.

But maybe they mean move core view classes out of `pathland-view-core` into `pathland-view-kotlin`, i.e. merge view vocabulary into the Kotlin DSL module, leaving pathland-view-core as engine/runtime only. That aligns with "remove all java dsl" and "core view classes moved to kotlin". However, the engine needs View (it emits View trees) so core depends on view. If View moves to pathland-view-kotlin, core would depend on Kotlin DSL, inverting dependency and making core not DSL-neutral. Unless they move *all* of pathland-view-core to Kotlin but keep module. The issue says keep pathland-view-core as engine/SPI. So "core view classes should be moved to kotlin" = rewrite them in Kotlin, still in pathland-view-core. Need to confirm.

Let me ask the user via question tool with options. But before, gather more: which modules depend on core from Java and would be affected by Kotlin conversion? Also whether the repo already has Kotlin compile configured in pathland-view-core (no). Check root pom Kotlin version.

/**
 * A small Kotlin-owned view that exercises persisted state, two-way text input,
 * reactive plain-Kotlin control flow, `ForEach`, and the Kotlin modifier sugar.
 */
class KotlinDemoView : KotlinView() {

    private var count by state(0)
    private val name = mutableState("", "demo.name")
    private var items by state(listOf("First item", "Second item"))

    override fun body(): View = VStack(spacing = 16f) {
        Text("Pathland Kotlin Demo")
            .fontSize(28f)
            .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)
        Text("SSR plus live 16-byte opcode deltas, authored in Kotlin.")

        HStack(spacing = 12f) {
            Text("Count: $count")
            Button("Increment") { count += 1 }
            Button("Reset") { count = 0 }
        }

        TextField("Your name", name)
        Text(computed { "Hello, ${name.value.ifBlank { "world" }}" })

        HStack(spacing = 12f) {
            Button("Add item") { items = items + "Item ${items.size + 1}" }
            Button("Clear items") { items = emptyList() }
        }

        ForEach(items) { item, _ -> Text("• $item") }
    }.padding(24).frame { maxWidth(720f) }
}

# pathland-demo-views — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

The remaining framework-agnostic **Java** demo views (`dev.pathland.demo`), consumed
by the Quarkus and Spring Boot demos. Uses `State` fields wired by the
`pathland-view-processor` annotation processor.

The music player moved to `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`; the shared demo theme and
assets moved to the DSL-neutral `pathland-demo-common` module.

## Implemented

- **`KitchenSinkView`** — a scrollable column of every protocol section.
- **Sections** — `SectionCard`, `CounterSection`, `TextFieldSection`,
  `ToggleSection`, `ValueControlsSection`, `PickerSection`, `ColorSection`,
  `DateSection`, `LayoutSection`, `TextStylesSection`, `AppearanceSection`, and
  `ThemeSection`.
- **Legacy views** — `CounterView`, `CounterControls`, `NameField`.
- **`SplitNavDemo`** — sidebar + detail navigation with `NavigationContainer`,
  route-driven window metadata, reactive active-row highlighting, and a fallback.
- **`AdView`** — the small sponsored-proxy origin app.
- **Semantic accessibility** — `MAIN`/`NAVIGATION`/`HEADER` roles; sidebar rows
  are real `Button`s; controls carry accessible labels.
- **Real asset refs** — icons use the semantic `Icon` primitive; non-icon media
  assets live in `pathland-demo-common`.
- **`DemoTheme` and `DemoAssets`** — now provided by `pathland-demo-common`.

## Not implemented / gaps

- The browser experience depends on the `@pathland/dom-renderer` client.
- These Java views remain a pre-1.0 porting target for Kotlin (#169).

## Verified by

`mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views` (JDK 17+) — `CounterViewTest`,
`KitchenSinkViewTest`, and `SplitNavDemoTest`.

# pathland-view-core (JVM engine) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine and runtime for the Pathland protocol.
It owns the `View` SPI and shared authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree
diff emitter, signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform
state, and JNA ring interop. The Java DSL (`pathland-view`) and the Kotlin DSL
(`pathland-view-kotlin`) are authoring layers over this module; server and
renderer modules depend on core only.

## Implemented

- **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`,
  `Commands`, `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`, `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`,
  `TokenPath`.
- **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`computed`/`effect`/
  `untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
  caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
  `Scheduler`.
- **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `State`/`PersistentState`,
  untyped `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Generated
  `<View>_StateBinder` classes are loaded from the view's own classloader, so
  application views keep working when a host loads the core in a parent
  extension classloader (Quarkus).
- **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
  `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
- **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
  `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
  `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` stays in the Java DSL because it composes `Button`.
- **JNA interop** (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`): lazy `PathlandCore` binding and
  `RingOpcodeSink` over `libpathland_core`.
- **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
  `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
  Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
  effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
  zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract.
- **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
  `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`, `Configurators`,
  `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
  `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
  wrappers.
- **Protocol manifest validation** (`ProtocolManifestTest`): the hand-written
  protocol constants (`Components`, `Properties`, `Commands`, `Categories`,
  `ValueTypes`) are checked against `spec/protocol.tsv` — including no extra
  public numeric constants and the full `ValueTypes.forProperty` mapping. No
  Java source is generated.
- **Shared engine traces**: `EngineTraceTest` (in `pathland-view`) runs the
  mount/text/property scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under
  `spec/engine-traces/`, byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in
  `spec/ENGINE.md`.
- **Test coverage**: the Java DSL module's test suite exercises the engine
  end-to-end (emitter/reconcile, signals, state, router, transport, JNA ring),
  plus the server/HTML/desktop consumers.

## Package boundary

- `pathland-view-core` is one Maven module for now: `core`/`engine` are logical
  subpackages inside it, with a few deliberate intra-module references
  (`Color`/`MediaController`/`Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting
  `core` and `engine` into separate artifacts requires a node SPI first.
- Production runtimes/renderers (`pathland-server-core`,
  `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-state-redis`, `pathland-test-kit`) depend on
  core, not on the Java DSL. Tests that author views through the DSL add
  `pathland-view` in test scope. The app-facing starters do depend on
  `pathland-view` because application code authors its root `View` with the DSL.

# pathland-gtk-demo (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

Runs the shared Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` (`dev.pathland.demo.music` from
`pathland-demo-views-kotlin`) under the **native GTK4 renderer**
(`libpathland_gtk`) — the cross-language, shared-renderer story for Java. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## How it works

- The Kotlin DSL mounts the view through its fine-grained `Emitter` into a
  `libpathland_core` shared ring (`RingOpcodeSink`, **zero-copy**).
- The in-process GTK renderer pumps the same ring in place
  (`pathland_gtk_run_ring`, via `PathlandCore.ringMut`); no
  `pathland-view-native` host is involved.
- Native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that this host drains
  (`pathland_core_drain_events`) and dispatches into the app's bindings via the
  shared `InputDispatcher` (taps, text/value/date inputs, **media events**,
  router back).
- State/theme/platform seeding mirrors the server session: `PersistentState`
  over an `InMemoryStateStore`, `DemoTheme.adaptive()` as the emitter theme.
- **App-driven media**: the renderer plays the demo's tracks through a direct
  GStreamer `playbin` (driven by the node's media control properties) and
  reports `MEDIA_*` events back through the ring. The app's web-style
  `/_pathland/assets/...` paths are resolved against a local asset root: the
  demo extracts its audio + covers from the shared `pathland-demo-common` jar at
  startup (`DemoAssets.extractToTemp`) and calls `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`.

## Implemented

Records are heavily accessed in Java tests. Using @JvmRecord preserves accessors. But note Kotlin @JvmRecord classes: can they have methods and companion? Yes. But `Opcode` has static `fromBytes` and `SIZE`; Kotlin companion with @JvmStatic gives `Opcode.fromBytes` and `@JvmField val SIZE` gives `Opcode.SIZE`. @JvmRecord is experimental requiring opt-in. Might be fine. Alternatively implement as Kotlin class with explicit functions named `category()` etc. to preserve Java API and also provide Kotlin properties? Can't have property `category` and function `category()` without JVM clash? getCategory vs category, no clash, but source usage in Kotlin would be ambiguous? `.category` property and `.category()` function both usable. Could do. But simplest: @JvmRecord.

However @JvmRecord restrictions: "The class must be a data class with all primary constructor parameters val; no mutable properties; cannot extend; cannot have inner classes; can have companion." I think okay. But `Color` record implements interfaces `View`, `TokenPath` and overrides `renderNode`; @JvmRecord allows member functions. Fine.

Engine `PathlandNode` is a class with public mutable fields. Kotlin `@JvmField var` preserves direct field access. Fine.

2. Move engine/runtime tests to core:

Careful about circular dependency: core cannot depend on pathland-view-kotlin. For RouterTest/RingOpcodeSinkTest/EngineTraceTest that currently use Java DSL, rewrite using core-only fixtures (implement View or build PathlandNode) to avoid core→DSL dependency. Or keep them in pathland-view-kotlin as they test integration. The issue says "Move engine/runtime tests from pathland-view into pathland-view-core" and "Run the shared engine traces through Kotlin". EngineTraceTest uses views; can live in pathland-view-kotlin as Kotlin test (tests engine through Kotlin DSL) — that's "run shared engine traces through Kotlin". RouterTest and RingOpcodeSinkTest could move to core with core-only fixtures, or to view-kotlin. Need choose.

   - RouterTest uses Java DSL heavily; port to view-kotlin (Kotlin DSL) or core-only. Router is core; NavigationContainer is core view. Could port to core with core Views built from PathlandNode? It uses Button/Text/BorderedButtonStyle/NavigationLink (Java DSL). Kotlin DSL has navigation helpers (NavigationLink? `NavigationLink` maybe in Navigation.kt). So port to view-kotlin as Kotlin; that validates router with Kotlin DSL.

Maybe create `pathland-test-kit` Kotlin `TestViews` helper in main so all modules can reuse? But test-kit is published. Could add to test scope? Simpler: each module's Kotlin test fixture.

Also remove `pathland-quarkus-java` from quarkus-demo dependency (Quarkus demo should use `pathland-quarkus` directly or `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`? It's a Java host mounting Kotlin views. ## New requirement: Java hosts must mount Kotlin-authored views

**Contract**
- `PathlandApp` stays a Java functional interface in `pathland-server-core`, returning the core `View`.
- Kotlin views compile to normal JVM bytecode; `pathland-view-kotlin` brings `kotlin-stdlib` transitively, so a Java Spring Boot/Quarkus app needs no Kotlin compiler to mount a Kotlin view that comes from a dependency.
- Every reusable Kotlin root/app view exposes a Java-callable entry point:
  - public no-arg constructor, or
  - `@JvmStatic fun make(...)` / `@JvmOverloads`, with Java-friendly parameter types only.
- `KotlinView` and all Kotlin DSL builders return `dev.pathland.view.core.View`; no Kotlin-only type appears in the mount path.
- Compile the Kotlinized core with `-Xjvm-default=all` so Java sees normal interface default methods.
- Host modules keep a clean split:
  - `pathland-spring-boot-starter` and `pathland-quarkus` production dependencies stay DSL-neutral.
  - The app adds `pathland-view-kotlin` (plus the module containing its Kotlin views).

**Proof/tests**
- `pathland-spring-boot-starter`: add a Java `KotlinViewMountTest` whose Java `@Configuration`/`TestApp` returns a `PathlandApp` calling a Kotlin test-fixture view. Assert SSR HTML contains the Kotlin view’s text and a signal delta updates it.
- `pathland-quarkus`: keep `CounterApp` as a Java CDI bean, but make `newRoot()` return a Kotlin-authored test-fixture view instead of a Java DSL view. Assert multi-session SSR/WS behavior.
- Kotlin fixtures use `@file:JvmName(...)` so Java call sites are stable and readable.
- Keep `pathland-quarkus-demo` and `pathland-spring-boot-demo` as living proof: both are Java hosts mounting the Kotlin `MusicPlayerView`; the Quarkus demo will also mount the Kotlin `AdView`.
- No Java DSL is reintroduced for this: mounting requires only `PathlandApp` + a Kotlin `View`.

**Where it lands**
- Phase 2: Kotlin fixtures + Java-host mount tests in the Spring Boot starter and Quarkus extension.
- Phase 3: keep starter/extension dependencies DSL-neutral; remove all remaining Java DSL references.
- Phase 4: apply the Java-callable API rules to the Kotlinized core.
- Phase 5: document the “Kotlin authors views, Java hosts mount them” contract in `README.md`, `spec/DSL.md`, and `AGENTS.md`.

**Additional acceptance criteria**
- A Java-only Spring Boot app with a `PathlandApp` bean and a Kotlin view dependency can SSR and receive live deltas.
- A Java-only Quarkus app can do the same.
- No Kotlin compiler is required in the Java host module itself.
- The starter/extension production classpaths contain neither `pathland-view` nor `pathland-view-kotlin`; Kotlin is an app/demo dependency.

--- .github/workflows/release.yml	
+++ .github/workflows/release.yml	
@@ -1,315 +1,313 @@
 name: Release
 
 # Publishing a GitHub Release (which creates the tag, e.g. `v0.1.1`) builds and
 # publishes every artifact — the Rust crates to crates.io and the Java libraries
 # to Maven Central (with the renderer's native libraries for every supported
 # platform) — then attaches the built files to the Release.
 #
 # The tag drives the version: the workflow writes the tag's `X.Y.Z` into the Rust
 # workspace version and the Java parent version (in CI only) before building, and
 # a `bump` job commits that version back to `main` afterwards. No pre-bump commit
 # is required. Tags must be `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (an optional pre-release
 # suffix is allowed).
 #
 # The publish steps are idempotent, so re-running a partially failed release is
 # safe (a crate+version already on crates.io is skipped; Maven Central rejects a
 # re-deploy of an existing version).
 #
 # Secrets:
 #   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN  crates.io API token (publish scope)
 #   GPG_PRIVATE_KEY       armored GPG private key (signing)
 #   GPG_PASSPHRASE        its passphrase
 #   CENTRAL_USERNAME      Sonatype Central Portal user token username
 #   CENTRAL_PASSWORD      Sonatype Central Portal user token password
 
 on:
   release:
     types: [published]
   workflow_dispatch:
     inputs:
       tag:
         description: 'Tag to release (e.g. v0.1.1); blank = current ref'
         required: false
 
 permissions:
   contents: write
 
 jobs:
   version:
     name: Resolve + validate version
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     outputs:
       tag: ${{ steps.v.outputs.tag }}
       version: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
     steps:
       - id: v
         name: Derive the version from the tag
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           tag="${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}"
           if [[ ! "$tag" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
             echo "::error::tag '$tag' must be v<major>.<minor>.<patch>"
             exit 1
           fi
           version="${tag#v}"
           echo "tag=$tag version=$version"
           echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
 
   rust:
     name: Publish crates to crates.io
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: version
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
       - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
 
       - name: Set the version from the tag
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           cargo install cargo-edit --locked
           cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
           # Sanity: the workspace version + the intra-workspace path-dep pins.
           awk -F'"' '/^version = /{print "workspace:", $2; exit}' Cargo.toml
           grep -rho 'pathland-[a-z-]*", version = "[^"]*"' crates/*/Cargo.toml | sort -u
 
       - name: Test the publishable crates
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: cargo test -p pathland-core -p pathland-engine -p pathland-view -p pathland-core-transport -p pathland-render-html
 
       - name: Publish in dependency order
         working-directory: lib/rust
         env:
           CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
           crates=(pathland-core pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html)
           for c in "${crates[@]}"; do
             echo "::group::publish $c $version"
             # Idempotent: skip a crate+version already on crates.io.
             if curl -sf -A "pathland-release-ci" "https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/$c/$version" >/dev/null; then
               echo "$c $version already published — skipping"
               echo "::endgroup::"
               continue
             fi
             # `cargo publish` packages (leaving the .crate in target/package) then uploads.
             # `--allow-dirty`: `cargo set-version` above intentionally edits the
             # crates' manifests (the path-dep version pins), so the tree is "dirty".
             cargo publish --allow-dirty -p "$c"
             echo "::endgroup::"
             # Let the index propagate so the next dependent crate resolves it.
             sleep 20
           done
 
       - name: Package (guarantee .crate files for the release assets)
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           # All dependencies are published by now, so packaging every crate works.
           for c in pathland-core pathland-engine pathland-view pathland-core-transport pathland-render-html; do
             cargo package --allow-dirty -p "$c"
           done
 
       - name: Upload the .crate files
         uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
         with:
           name: crates
           path: lib/rust/target/package/*.crate
           if-no-files-found: error
 
   java-natives:
     name: Build renderer natives (${{ matrix.platform }})
     runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
     needs: version
     strategy:
       fail-fast: false
       matrix:
         include:
           - { platform: windows-x86_64, runner: windows-latest }
           - { platform: linux-x86_64, runner: ubuntu-latest }
           - { platform: linux-aarch64, runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm }
           - { platform: macos-aarch64, runner: macos-14 }
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
       - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
 
       - name: Build the renderer cdylib
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: cargo build --release -p pathland-render-html
 
       - name: Stage the platform lib
         shell: bash
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           case "${{ matrix.platform }}" in
             windows-*) src="pathland_render_html.dll";      dst="libpathland_render_html.dll" ;;
             macos-*)   src="libpathland_render_html.dylib"; dst="libpathland_render_html.dylib" ;;
             *)         src="libpathland_render_html.so";    dst="libpathland_render_html.so" ;;
           esac
           dest="lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/${{ matrix.platform }}"
           mkdir -p "$dest"
           cp "lib/rust/target/release/$src" "$dest/$dst"
           ls -la "$dest"
 
       - name: Upload the platform lib
         uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
         with:
           name: native-${{ matrix.platform }}
           path: lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/${{ matrix.platform }}/*
           if-no-files-found: error
 
   java:
     name: Publish to Maven Central
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: [version, java-natives]
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
 
       - name: Set up JDK + Maven credentials + GPG
         uses: actions/setup-java@v4
         with:
           distribution: temurin
           java-version: '17'
           cache: maven
           server-id: central
           server-username: CENTRAL_USERNAME
           server-password: CENTRAL_PASSWORD
           gpg-private-key: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
           gpg-passphrase: MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE
 
       # Maven 3.10 (the runner default since 2026-10-04) writes a
       # `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
       # which central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles and the Portal rejects
       # ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). 3.9.x does not. Pin it here.
       - name: Pin Maven 3.9.9
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           v=3.9.9
           curl -sSL "https://archive.apache.org/dist/maven/maven-3/$v/binaries/apache-maven-$v-bin.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$HOME"
           echo "$HOME/apache-maven-$v/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
           mvn -v
 
       - name: Set the version from the tag
         working-directory: lib/java
         run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true
 
       - name: Download the platform natives
         uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
         with:
           path: natives
 
       - name: Stage the natives for the jar embed
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           mkdir -p lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native
           for d in natives/native-*; do
             platform="${d#natives/native-}"
             mkdir -p "lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/$platform"
             cp "$d"/* "lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/$platform/"
           done
           find lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native -type f
 
       # The demos are excluded from the release reactor: central-publishing-maven-plugin
       # bundles every reactor module (it ignores maven.deploy.skip), and the demos must
       # not be published.
       - name: Deploy to Maven Central
         working-directory: lib/java
         env:
           CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
           CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
           MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
         run: >-
           mvn -B -P release deploy
-          -pl '!pathland-demo-common,!pathland-demo-views-kotlin,!pathland-demo-views,!pathland-gtk-demo,!pathland-qt-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'
+          -pl '!pathland-demo-common,!pathland-demo-views-kotlin,!pathland-gtk-demo,!pathland-qt-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'
 
       - name: Collect the published main jars
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           mkdir -p dist/jars
-          for m in pathland-view-core pathland-view pathland-view-processor pathland-view-kotlin \
+          for m in pathland-view-core pathland-view-kotlin \
                    pathland-render-html pathland-state-redis pathland-server-core \
                    pathland-observability pathland-test-kit pathland-spring-boot-starter \
                    pathland-quarkus pathland-quarkus-deployment \
-                   pathland-quarkus-java pathland-quarkus-java-deployment \
-                   pathland-quarkus-kotlin pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment \
-                   pathland-quarkus-starter; do
+                   pathland-quarkus-kotlin pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment; do
             cp lib/java/"$m"/target/"$m"-*.jar dist/jars/ 2>/dev/null || true
           done
           rm -f dist/jars/*-sources.jar dist/jars/*-javadoc.jar
           ls -la dist/jars
 
       - name: Upload the main jars
         uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
         with:
           name: jars
           path: dist/jars/*.jar
           if-no-files-found: error
 
   bump:
     name: Commit the version back to main
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: [version, rust, java]
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
         with:
           ref: main
           fetch-depth: 0
 
       - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
       - name: Set the Rust version
         working-directory: lib/rust
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           cargo install cargo-edit --locked
           cargo set-version --workspace "${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
 
       - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
         with:
           distribution: temurin
           java-version: '17'
       - name: Set the Java version
         working-directory: lib/java
         run: mvn -B -q versions:set -DnewVersion="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}" -DgenerateBackupPoms=false -DprocessAllModules=true
 
       - name: Commit + push
         run: |
           set -euo pipefail
           git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
           git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
           if git diff --quiet; then
             echo "version already current on main — nothing to commit"
             exit 0
           fi
           git add -A
           git commit -m "chore(release): v${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
           git push origin HEAD:main
 
   release-assets:
     name: Attach release assets
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     needs: [version, rust, java-natives, java]
     steps:
       - name: Download all build artifacts
         uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
         with:
           path: dist
 
       - name: Collect the files to attach

       - name: Attach to the GitHub Release

 # Pathland Project - AI Agent Guide
 
 This document provides essential context for AI agents (or human contributors) working on the **Pathland** protocol. It captures the project's direction, architectural decisions, and implementation details to ensure consistency.
 
 **Last Updated**: November 3, 2026
 
 ---
 
 ## Architecture: Rust Opcode Engine
 
 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine** that emits the application's
 > **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding,
 > alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared linear
 > memory, consumed by host renderers. View components and modifiers are written
-> in Rust with a SwiftUI-like API, and in Java with the hand-written
-> **`dev.pathland.view` DSL** (reusable library, Java 17+); both drive the engine
-> through the flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared
-> ring on desktop.
+> in Rust with a SwiftUI-like API, and in Kotlin with the hand-written
+> **`dev.pathland.view.dsl` DSL** (reusable JVM library, Java 17+); both drive the
+> engine through the flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a
+> zero-copy shared ring on desktop. Java hosts mount Kotlin views through
+> `PathlandApp`.
 
 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Both directions are binary**: a second **event ring** (host → guest) carries `EVENT`-category opcodes. The renderer writes raw inputs at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains them at `eventReadCursor`. Events are 16-byte opcodes through the engine, never a side-channel callback.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes. A second host-owned **event arena** mirrors this in the host → guest direction (shared-memory event strings, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED`); over the network, host → guest strings ride the batch's string section.
 - **Window metadata** (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`, field family `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION`/`LOCALE`) carries the hosting surface's presentation metadata; renderers map it to their own chrome (browser `<title>`/meta description/`<html lang>`, GTK/Qt window title). It is root-scoped and signal-backed, so a route title is a computed over the router. Web-only artifacts (canonical/robots/sitemap) stay host-owned.
 - Spec: **`spec/OPCODE.md`** (primary) + **`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`** (golden vectors). Companion catalogs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** (views), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (modifiers/properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (events), **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract) — draft IDs are allocated there spec-first.
 
 ### Declarative, not positioned (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The engine describes WHAT the UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
 > padding, alignment — never WHERE it is. It does not compute layout and does
 > not emit rects.**
 
 - The engine emits **declarative structure** (`TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move) + **constraint properties** (`PARAMETER` spacing/padding/alignment/FILL/HUG hints).
 - **Native elements everywhere**: each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the browser, HTML server-side — and those native elements lay themselves out. Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 - **Reactive emission**: emission is diff-based. Only the nodes that changed emit opcodes (property diffs via `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`, structural diffs via `TREE` opcodes). An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. Signals in the application mark the tree dirty; the engine reconciles.
 - **Zero dynamic heap allocations** during steady-state emission (proven by test).
 
 ### no_std / wasm32 direction guard (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 `pathland-core` and `pathland-view` must remain `#![no_std]` + `alloc` and
 compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. This is the guarantee that the protocol
 core can still target a browser / embedded / remote projection later (goal #15,
 Quarkus SSR + WebSocket). The desktop path (`pathland-view-native`) is the only
 consumer today, but the core must not become desktop-only. Verify with
 `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` (i.e. `cargo build -p pathland-core -p pathland-view
 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`).
 
 ### Reactive signals (Angular-style)
 
 `pathland-core::signal` provides writable signals that live in the engine. A
 node binds its text (`Node::text_binding`), a property
 (`Node::property_bindings`) or a **string property** (`Node::string_bindings`,
 e.g. a media controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) to a `SignalId`; during emit the engine
 resolves the binding and records the dependency, and `Engine::set_signal`
 re-emits **only the bound nodes** (`SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY`) — no full tree
 walk. Signal values
 are one of `F32`/`U32`/`Bool`/`Enum`/`Str` (packed to the wire's `u32` value or
 arena string). Foreign hosts reach signals via the flat C ABI
 (`pathland_native_signal_create_*` / `signal_set_*` / `node_bind_text` /
 `node_bind_property`) and the Java `Signal` type. Binding then calling `emit`
 records the dependency; a subsequent `set` is a partial emit. (Computed/derived
 signals + effects are the planned next step.)

 ### HTML base design (`design/`)
 
 The HTML renderer's built-in stylesheet is generated from a **three-layer Style
 Dictionary pipeline** plus hand-authored reset/component CSS (one built-in base
 design; no app-facing base-design selection):
 
 ```
 design/tokens/base/*.tokens.json      # internal palette + scales (not emitted)
 design/tokens/semantic/*.tokens.json  # protocol catalog semantics (emitted)
 design/tokens/component/*.tokens.json # per-component surface (emitted)
 design/html/{reset,components}.css    # hand-authored CSS consuming var(--pl-*)
 design/scripts/{build,dev,check}.mjs  # SD build, watcher/preview, validation
 design/build/base.css                 # generated: reset + tokens + components
 design/build/base.css.name            # content hash: base-<sha256-12>.css
 ```
 
 - Tokens are flat DTCG entries (`$value`/`$type`/`$extensions.pathland`) because
   the catalog has both leaf and group paths (`control.border` vs
   `control.border.width`). Dark values live on `$extensions.pathland.dark`;
   durations/z-index/`em` icon sizes are marked internal.
 - `npm --prefix design run build` generates
   `design/build/{tokens.css,manifest.json,base.css,base.css.name}`;
   `npm --prefix design run check` validates catalog coverage, layer direction,
   dark/forced-dark declarations, dimension/`isLengthToken` rules, and the CSS
   content hash.
 - `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` copies the bundle + name to
   `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/` (committed; `--check` fails on
   drift). `css.rs` embeds both with `include_str!` (`builtin_css()` /
   `builtin_css_name()`).
 - The renderer's library default is inline (`render_document`); the linked mode
   (`render_document_linked`, C ABI `pathland_html_render_linked` +
   `pathland_html_base_css[_name]`, Java `renderLinked`/`baseCss`/`baseCssName`)
   emits `{base}/base-<hash>.css`. The Spring Boot and Quarkus starters use it
   and serve the renderer-owned bytes immutable (global + mounted bases); token
   overrides/fit rules stay inline.
 - `scripts/lib.sh` (`build_rust_html`), the Maven `refresh-ide` profile, and CI
   run the design build + sync. Do not edit generated CSS by hand.

 ### GTK4 Renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`)
 
 The desktop renderer: a single crate that owns **all** GTK/glib/pango usage and
 maps opcode frames **incrementally** onto native GTK widgets (a retained
 `id → gtk::Widget` map). Both the Rust demo and the Java demo render through
 it — the demos **never call GTK or Swing directly**:
 
 - Rust demo links `pathland-render-gtk` as an `rlib` and calls `GtkRenderer::run(...)`
   with a wake closure.
 - Java demo (`pathland-gtk-demo`) loads `pathland-render-gtk` as a `cdylib` via JNA and
   calls `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` over the Kotlin view's
   `libpathland_core` ring; native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes through the shared
   ring. The renderer **writes** the events and **wakes** the host (no payload); the host
   drains the event ring itself via `pathland_core_drain_events`. Events are never
   delivered through a side-channel callback — they flow through the opcode engine.
   The demo mounts the Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` (the same shared view the web demos use) with the
   app-driven media contract: the renderer plays the tracks through a direct GStreamer
   `playbin` and reports `MEDIA_*` events back; the demo's web-style
   `/_pathland/assets/...` paths resolve against an extracted local asset root
   (`pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`).
 
 The renderer maps native inputs onto the raw `Event` surface via GTK4
 controllers (`Button::clicked` → pointer up, `EventControllerMotion` →
 pointer move/enter/leave), emitting events through the same `Pump::send_input`
 path.
 
 `pathland_gtk::run` passes an explicit empty argv to GTK (the process command
 line belongs to the embedding host — e.g. the JVM's `-cp`/`-D` flags — and must
 not be parsed as GTK options).

 ## Project Vision
 
 **Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol** that enables retained-mode UI development with multiple renderer backends. It is **protocol-first**, meaning the protocol specification is the source of truth, not any particular implementation.
 
 **Primary Goal**: Write once, run anywhere - Enable UI code to be written once and deployed across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded platforms through different renderer implementations.
 
 **Status**: The Rust opcode engine (16-byte opcode, ring buffer, arena, diff-based reactive emission) is implemented and tested (`cargo test`). See the Architecture section above.
 
 ---
 
 ## CRITICAL ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES
 
 ### Principle 1: Renderer Statelessness (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The renderer MUST NOT retain application state.**
 
 - Renderers are **pure functions** of the opcode stream: same opcodes → same output
 - A renderer MAY retain its **rendered-output tree** (id → native element + computed layout) for drawing, hit-testing, and event routing — this is a cache of its own output, not state
 - The renderer MUST NOT retain component property values as business state, application control flow, or anything the application can change without emitting an opcode
 - The application owns the canonical retained UI tree
 - The engine emits **deltas only**; the renderer applies them to its native elements
 
 **Violation of this principle is a bug, not a feature.**
 
 ### Principle 2: Command-Based Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol transmits tree mutations as a stream of commands, NOT as serialized trees.**
 
 - Each frame is a **batch of delta commands** describing changes
 - Only **actual changes** are transmitted (diff-based reactive emission)
 - Protocol acts like a **VM instruction stream** / ABI
 - Deterministic, linear decoding without schema lookup or reflection
 
 ### Principle 3: Binary Protocol (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The protocol MUST be binary.**
 
 - Open-source, cross-platform binary format
 - Fixed **16-byte instructions** in a ring buffer shared with the host via linear memory
 - Custom instruction-based bytecode, not schema-driven serialization
 - **Both directions are binary**: tree mutations (app → renderer) AND raw-input events (renderer → app) share the same instruction format, so the wire is language- and platform-agnostic

 ### Opcode Format
 
 Every opcode is exactly 16 bytes:
 
 ```
 [Category: u8][Command: u8][Flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
 ```
 
 See `spec/OPCODE.md` for the full format, ring buffer, arena, and frame lifecycle.
 
 ### Machine-readable protocol manifest
 
 `spec/protocol.tsv` is the target-neutral ID manifest emitted from
 `pathland_core::constants` by `pathland-protocol-manifest` (`cargo run -p
 pathland-protocol-manifest`). It contains only `kind`, `group`, `name`, and
 `value`; each language binding keeps its own representation and validates or
 reads the manifest. There is no Rust→Java source generation.
 
 The JVM mirror is hand-written and checked by
 `pathland-view-core/src/test/java/.../ProtocolManifestTest`: every manifest row
 must match a Java constant, no extra public numeric constants may exist, and
 `ValueTypes.forProperty` must match `property_value_type`. CI regenerates the
 manifest from Rust and fails on drift.
 
 Engine behavior beyond individual opcodes is specified in `spec/ENGINE.md` and
 enforced by shared self-contained frame traces under `spec/engine-traces/`.
 `pathland-engine-golden` emits them from the Rust engine and the JVM
 `EngineTraceTest` compares its encoded frames byte-for-byte.
 
 ### Categories
 
 | Category | Value | Direction | Description |
 |----------|-------|-----------|-------------|
 | TREE | 0x01 | Guest → Host | Node create/delete/insert/remove/move |
 | PARAMETER | 0x02 | Guest → Host | Constraint properties (spacing, padding, …), design tokens |
 | EVENT | 0x03 | Host → Guest | Raw inputs: pointer down/move/up, key down/up |
 | META | 0x04 | Both | Reset, environment, window metadata |

 ### Key Property IDs
 
 **Stack**: SPACING=0x0001, ALIGNMENT=0x0002, CONTENT_MARGINS=0x0005

 ### Colors
 
 - Literal colors are **sRGB** with D65 white point, packed as `0xAARRGGBB`
 - A color property may instead carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path
 - Semantic token resolution and theme adaptation are **renderer-owned**
 
 ### Design Token System
 
 **Core Principle**: Application defines intent, overrides, and the theme.
 Renderer defines visual appearance, behavior, defaults, and interaction states.
 
-- The **application owns the theme**: token overrides (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**) and token references in style properties. Token refs cover COLOR and non-color values (`Length` for spacing/padding/font size/radius/border/frame; `FontFamily.Token` for STRING) in the Rust and Java DSLs.
+- The **application owns the theme**: token overrides (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**) and token references in style properties. Token refs cover COLOR and non-color values (`Length` for spacing/padding/font size/radius/border/frame; `FontFamily.Token` for STRING) in the Rust and Kotlin DSLs.
 - The **renderer owns** default token values (light + dark, the full Tier-1 catalog), token resolution (including explicit `dark.` = forced dark and parent fallback), effective color-scheme detection, interaction states (hover, pressed, focus, disabled), and theme adaptation
 - `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` identifies tokens by **dot-separated string paths** (e.g. `color.primary`, `space.2`) with the standard value-type encoding — there is no separate numeric tokenId system. A `dark.` prefix selects the dark variant (`dark.color.primary`); a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference whose path starts with `dark.` forces the dark value in either scheme
 - **Runtime theming**: `META::RESET_THEME` clears every app override; a replacement theme is reset + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides in one frame. `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` forces `platform`/`light`/`dark`. Both are renderer state — no node is re-emitted. Java: `Emitter.replaceTheme`/`setColorScheme` + `PathlandSession.setTheme`/`setColorScheme`; Rust: `Engine::reset_theme`/`set_color_scheme`.
 - An unresolvable token reference leaves the property **unset** (renderer default), never an error or stale value.
 - The protocol MUST NEVER describe hover styles, click styles, visual transitions, conditional styling, or layout tuning for interaction states
 - **Deferred**: applying per-component tokens to native GTK/Qt leaf control chrome; web parent-path fallback.
 
 The HTML renderer's default token values are generated from `design/` (see
 "HTML base design" above). Full details: [Design Token System](./spec/OPCODE.md#design-token-system)
 and the canonical catalog / color-scheme contract in [spec/TOKENS.md](./spec/TOKENS.md).

 ## Implementation Guidelines
 
 ### Adding New Component
 1. Add to `component_type` in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Implement the component type in `pathland-core` (if it affects the retained tree)
 4. Implement native-element mapping in the target renderer (Goal 3–5)
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Adding New Property
 1. Add to the appropriate property module in `constants.rs`
 2. Document in `spec/OPCODE.md`
 3. Handle the value type in `pathland-core`'s diff emission (if a stack/text/size property)
 4. Implement in each renderer's property application
 5. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Modifying Protocol
 1. Update `spec/OPCODE.md` first (and `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` vectors)
 2. Update `constants.rs` and `pathland-core` encoding/emitters
 3. Run `cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest` and commit the
    updated `spec/protocol.tsv`
 4. Update the hand-written JVM protocol constants (the Java manifest test fails
    with the exact missing/stale row otherwise)
 5. If emission behavior changed, run
    `cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit` and commit the trace fixtures
 6. Verify backward compatibility; update `pathland-core`/renderers + tests
 7. Update the affected project(s)' `status.md`
 
 ### Changing the Wire Format
 - Bump the wire `version` field in `spec/OPCODE.md` and `pathland-core`'s header (currently 1). Pre-release format changes are acceptable while version stays 1.
 
 ### Keeping implementation status updated (MANDATORY)
 
 **The agent MUST keep the per-project `status.md` files in sync with the code.**
 Whenever you land a protocol or renderer change — a new component/property/
 command/event, a new encoder/decoder, a new widget mapping, a new modifier or
 renderer feature, a test that proves new surface — **update the affected
 project's `status.md`** (Implemented / Not implemented / gaps) in the same
 change. The specs (`spec/`) describe the protocol contract only and MUST NOT
 carry implementation status; status lives in `status.md` next to each
 implementing project.

 ## Common Pitfalls
 
 ### NEVER Do These
 | Anti-Pattern | Why Wrong | Correct |
 |--------------|-----------|---------|
 | Renderer stores application state | Violates statelessness | Application owns the tree |
 | Engine computes layout / emits rects | Violates declarative model | Emit structure + constraints; native elements lay out |
 | Send full trees | Inefficient | Diff-based reactive emission |
 | String property names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | String component names | Larger payloads | Use numeric IDs |
 | Generic RGB | Ambiguous | Explicitly sRGB |
 | Hover styles in protocol | Renderer job | Define in theme |
 | Heap allocation in steady-state emission | Slow | Preallocated snapshot slab + arena |

 ## Pathland Mindset
 
 **Always remember**:
 1. Protocol is King
 2. Renderers are Dumb (execute commands only)
 3. Applications are Smart (generate commands)
 4. Only Changes Matter (transmit mutations / reactive emission)
 5. Binary is Beautiful (efficient, deterministic)

Your view declaration compiles to fixed 16-byte opcodes that any renderer applies to native elements. The wire is the contract: a view written in Java, Rust, C#, or anything else produces the **same opcode stream**, and any renderer can apply it. That makes Pathland **language- and renderer-agnostic**: - **Write the UI once, declaratively.** A SwiftUI-shaped DSL in your language of choice — Java, Rust, C#, anything — describes the same view structure, whatever it later runs on. - **Run it on any surface.** The same view code drives today's server-rendered web and the native GTK4 desktop renderer, and is on track for the browser via WASM, embedded chips (LVGL), and native mobile/desktop (SwiftUI/UIKit, Jetpack Compose, Qt) ([Where it's headed](#where-its-headed)). - **Only changes travel.** The protocol is a stream of tiny binary deltas: an unchanged screen transmits zero bytes, and updates are applied in place. **Server-side rendering is the first surface we ship** — the flagship getting-started path — **not the whole story**. Browser — SSR + live WebSocket deltas
Desktop — native GTK4 renderer

You write the **whole UI in your backend language** — Java, C#, Rust, anything. Pathland renders the first page as server-side HTML, so it appears instantly, then keeps it alive with tiny binary updates over a WebSocket. The result is a smooth, reactive UI — delivered by the backend team, without npm, bundlers, an extra build pipeline, or a separate frontend. ``` You declare the UI in your backend │ ▼ The server renders it (HTML) and owns it │ ▼ Only the things that change travel to the client │ ▼ The client applies them to native elements (60FPS) ``` - **You declare the UI** with a SwiftUI-shaped DSL — `VStack`, `Text`, `Button`, styling — right next to your business logic. - **The server renders and owns it.** The first page is plain HTML (instant paint, SEO-friendly); the server keeps the authoritative copy of the UI. - **Only changes travel.** A click, a signal update, a navigation — the server sends a few tiny binary bytes describing exactly what changed. An unchanged screen sends nothing. The client applies them to real native elements (browser DOM, GTK widgets), so the platform does the layout, animation, and accessibility. ## The whole app Add one dependency and one bean, and you have a working app. **Spring Boot** ```java @SpringBootApplication public class MyApp { public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(MyApp.class, args); Java +hosts only need `dev.pathland.server.PathlandApp` and a Kotlin view factory.)* ## What it removes Today's server team pays for a BFF, a client-side state model, a SPA framework, and a JS build toolchain — all to render UI the server already owns. Pathland removes that layer: the backend *is* the application. There is no frontend contract to maintain, no client state model, and no JavaScript to write — and the same backend code that serves the web can drive other renderers later. ## Why it's smooth Pathland is built for smooth 60FPS UIs: - **Only changes are sent.** A screen that isn't changing transmits zero bytes. Updates are tiny binary deltas, not re-rendered pages or JSON trees. - **Native elements, not a canvas.** The platform lays out and animates real elements — you get native layout, text rendering, and accessibility for free, whether those elements are DOM nodes or GTK widgets. - **A thin client.** The web client is a small static file that hydrates the server HTML and applies updates in place. Write the app logic once, run it on embedded, mobile, desktop, and browser. Pathland is an open protocol, so the same code that drives the server-rendered UI today can also run on the device itself: - **In the browser**, the app logic compiles to WASM, writes to a shared buffer, and the main thread is left to rendering alone. - **On embedded devices**, the logic runs on one core while another core renders, with the ring buffer carrying the protocol between them — mapped onto a lightweight UI toolkit like LVGL. - **On mobile and desktop**, the same logic drives native renderers — SwiftUI/UIKit on Apple platforms, Jetpack Compose on Android, Qt and GTK on desktop.  # Releasing Pathland
 
 Publishing a **GitHub Release** (tagged `vX.Y.Z`) runs
 `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which sets the version from the tag, builds and
 publishes every artifact, attaches the built files to the Release, and commits
 the version back to `main`:
 
 | Ecosystem | Artifacts | Registry |
 |-----------|-----------|----------|
 | Rust | `pathland-core`, `pathland-engine`, `pathland-view`, `pathland-core-transport`, `pathland-render-html` | crates.io |
 | Java | `dev.pathland:*` libraries (incl. the renderer's native libs for windows-x86_64, linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64) | Maven Central |
 
 ## Versioning (tag-driven)
 
 **The tag drives the version** — no pre-bump commit is needed:
 
 - The workflow writes `X.Y.Z` (from the tag `vX.Y.Z`) into
   `lib/rust/Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package] version` + the intra-workspace
   path-dep pins, via `cargo set-version --workspace`) and
   `lib/java/pom.xml` (via `mvn versions:set`) **in CI**, then publishes.
 - A `bump` job then commits that version back to `main`, so `main` always
   reflects the latest release.
 
 Tags must be `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (an optional pre-release suffix is
 allowed); the `version` job fails on anything else. Releases are immutable per
 version — pick a new tag to re-release.
 
 ## One-time setup
 
 Repository secrets (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions):
 
 - `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` — a crates.io API token with publish scope
   (https://crates.io/settings/tokens).
 - `GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` — an armored GPG private key whose public key is on a
   keyserver (Central verifies the signatures).
 - `GPG_PASSPHRASE` — that key's passphrase.
 - `CENTRAL_USERNAME` / `CENTRAL_PASSWORD` — a Sonatype Central Portal **user
   token** (https://central.sonatype.com/account).
 
 Also: `main` must be pushable by the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (the `bump` job).
 If `main` is protected, allow the Actions bot, or the bump step fails (after a
 successful publish).
 
 ## Release
 
 1. Create a **GitHub Release** on `main` tagged `vX.Y.Z` (publish it).
 2. The workflow runs:
    - `version` — derive + validate `X.Y.Z` from the tag.
    - `rust` — set the version, test the publishable crates, publish them to
      crates.io in dependency order, upload the `.crate` files.
    - `java-natives` — build `libpathland_render_html` for windows-x86_64,
      linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64.
     - `java` — set the version, stage the natives into the renderer jar, run
       `mvn -P release deploy` to Maven Central (auto-published after validation).
     - `bump` — commit the version back to `main`.
     - `release-assets` — attach the `.crate` files, the Java main jars, and the
       four native libs to the GitHub Release.
 
 The Java deploy runs on **Maven 3.9.9** (pinned in the workflow): Maven 3.10
 writes a `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
 which the Portal rejects ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). The demos
-are **excluded from the release reactor** (`-pl '!pathland-demo-common,!pathland-demo-views-kotlin,!pathland-demo-views,!pathland-gtk-demo,!pathland-qt-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'`)
+are **excluded from the release reactor** (`-pl '!pathland-demo-common,!pathland-demo-views-kotlin,!pathland-gtk-demo,!pathland-qt-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'`)
 — `central-publishing-maven-plugin` bundles every reactor module, ignoring
 `maven.deploy.skip`, and the demos must not be published.
 
 The publish steps are **idempotent**: a crate+version already on crates.io is
 skipped, so re-running a partially failed release is safe (re-run the workflow
 via `workflow_dispatch`, passing the `tag`). Maven Central rejects a re-deploy of
 an existing version, so a Java re-run only helps if the Java deploy did not
 complete.
 
 ## Local pre-flight
 
 Rust — `cargo publish --dry-run -p pathland-core` validates the leaf crate (the
 dependent crates can only be dry-run once their dependencies are on crates.io,
 so the ordered CI publish validates them).
 
 Java — `mvn -P release verify` builds and signs the sources/javadoc jars without
 uploading. It needs GPG installed and a `central` server in `~/.m2/settings.xml`:
 
 ```xml
 <server>
   <id>central</id>
   <username>TOKEN_USERNAME</username>
   <password>TOKEN_PASSWORD</password>
 </server>
 ```
 
 ## Publishable crates (dependency order)
 
 ```
 pathland-core → pathland-engine → pathland-view → pathland-core-transport → pathland-render-html
 ```
 
 (`pathland-view-native`, `pathland-core-capi`, `pathland-render-gtk`,
 `pathland-render-gtk-demo`, `pathland-html-golden`, `pathland-ts-codegen` are
 **not** published — C-ABI cdylibs, the GTK renderer, and dev tools.)

-`pathland-view-kotlin`, `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-state-redis`,

-`pathland-quarkus-java`, `pathland-quarkus-java-deployment`,
-`pathland-quarkus-kotlin`, `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment`,
-`pathland-quarkus-starter` (plus the `pathland-parent` POM). The demo modules
+`pathland-quarkus-kotlin`, `pathland-quarkus-kotlin-deployment`
+(plus the `pathland-parent` POM). The demo modules

-`pathland-demo-views`, `pathland-gtk-demo`, `pathland-qt-demo`,
+`pathland-gtk-demo`, `pathland-qt-demo`,

 # Security Policy
 
 Pathland is a network-facing binary protocol: the byte decoders and the C ABI
 are security-critical surfaces. This policy covers how vulnerabilities are
 reported and handled.
 
 ## Reporting a vulnerability
 
 **Do not open a public issue for a security vulnerability.** Report it privately
 to the maintainers:
 
 - Email: `michael@apaq.dk`
 - Subject prefix: `[Pathland security]`
 
 Please include:
 
 - The affected crate/module and version (or commit).
 - A description of the vulnerability and its impact.
 - A minimal reproduction (payload bytes or code) where possible.
 - Any suggested fix, if you have one.
 
 We aim to acknowledge reports within **5 business days** and to ship a fix (or a
 mitigation) as soon as a coordinated patch is ready. We will credit reporters in
 the release notes unless anonymity is requested.
 
 ## Scope
 
 The following are in scope for this policy:
 
 - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core` — the `no_std` protocol core (opcode decode,
   ring buffer, arena, memory layout).
 - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-transport` — PLPL batch encode/decode.
 - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core-capi` — the `unsafe extern "C"` ring ABI
   (`libpathland_core`): pointer-argument handling, zero-copy reads, event drain.
-- `lib/java/pathland-view` `transport` — `FrameCodec` (PLPL encode/decode).
+- `lib/java/pathland-view-core` `transport` — `FrameCodec` (PLPL encode/decode).
 - The `@pathland/dom-renderer` web client (PLPL batch decode + hydration in
   `lib/typescript/src`, built to `dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` and copied into
   both demos).
 
 Out of scope: dependencies (report those to their respective projects),
 development-only tooling, and the demo application code.
 
 ## Security-sensitive guarantees
 
 - Every 16-byte opcode decoder must **reject malformed/truncated input
   gracefully** (no panics, no out-of-bounds reads, no hangs) — see the hardening
   issues (#37, #38).
 - The C ABI entry points (`pathland_ring_buffer_push`,
   `pathland_core_arena_alloc`, `pathland_core_drain_events`, …) treat
   caller-provided pointers as trusted by contract; the bounds guarantees must be
   upheld and are audited via Miri/sanitizers in CI.
 - No secrets or tokens may ever be committed; see
   [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md).
 
 ## Security testing
 
 Coverage is tracked by the hardening milestone (issues #37–#39): fuzzing for the
 Rust/TypeScript/Java decoders, Miri + ASan/UBSan on the C ABI, and bounds fixes.
 Results will be linked here as they land.
 
 ## Supported versions
 
 The project is pre-1.0 (`wire protocol version 1`). Security fixes land on the
 default branch and are backported only when a tagged release is actively used;
 see the [Versioning](README.md#versioning) section.

 ## 2. Problem
 
 Server-driven UI (SDUI) and cross-platform UI are fragmented: each platform
 re-invents retained-mode UI inside a closed framework (Flutter, React Native,
 Compose Multiplatform, per-vendor SDUI like Airbnb/Lyft/Spotify). The result:
 
 - **No open, language- and platform-agnostic *protocol*** exists for describing
   declarative, retained-mode UI — only frameworks that couple the UI model to a
   specific runtime.
 - **No single wire format** serves the full spectrum from embedded
   microcontrollers to in-browser to server-driven enterprise apps, so teams
   build and maintain N different UI transports.
 - **Full-tree serialization is wasteful**: typical SDUI re-sends large JSON
   payloads; large, reactive trees cannot sustain high frame rates on the wire or
   on the main thread.
 - **Enterprise cost of rich clients**: teams pay for a BFF, a separate frontend
   application, a client-side state model, and a JS toolchain — and still expose
   REST APIs and JWT tokens to the browser, maintain two languages across the
   stack (Java + TypeScript), and struggle with microfrontends and bundle size.
   This is the pain the applicant lives with daily at an enterprise (SOS
   International).
 
 ## 3. Innovation — a standard, not another framework
 
 Today's popular UI frameworks never re-invent themselves, and stay locked to
 running everything on the main thread. Pathland separates the declarative UI
 model from the renderer with a **binary protocol**, and does **signal-based
 change detection inside the model**. That yields both better performance than
 existing web frameworks and the flexibility to use **any language for any
 renderer on any device**.
 
 Pathland describes **WHAT** the UI is — structure + constraint properties
 (VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment) — as a stream of **fixed
 16-byte opcodes** in a ring buffer, and never **WHERE** (no layout, no rects).
 Renderers are **pure functions of the stream**, so the same opcode stream maps
 onto native widgets on every platform (GTK4, DOM/HTML, embedded-planned).
 
 The engine is **transport- and process-agnostic**: the producer and consumer
 only need to exchange bytes, so it runs identically across embedded dual-core,
 pure in-browser (WASM), native desktop (C ABI / JNA over a zero-copy shared
 ring), and distributed server-driven modes.
 
 **Emission is diff-based and reactive**: a signal bound to a node re-emits only
 that node's deltas; an unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. That is what makes
 the binary format dramatically smaller than JSON SDUI and fast enough for a
 120 FPS interaction target.
 
 The open-standard angle: anyone can implement a Pathland renderer or DSL in any
 language against the spec and the golden conformance vectors, with no lock-in to
 a runtime.
 
 ## 4. The specification (exists — split, not monolithic)
 
 The normative spec is **already present** and is the contract this proposal
 matures:

 |------|---------|
 | `spec/OPCODE.md` | 16-byte opcode format, ring buffer, arena, frame lifecycle, value types, design tokens |
 | `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` | Primitive views + component IDs |
 | `spec/MODIFIERS.md` | Core modifiers/properties + value types + enum codes |
 | `spec/EVENTS.md` | Core events + listener bits |
 | `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` | Golden byte vectors |
 | `spec/DSL.md` | Authoring surface (SwiftUI-shaped DSL contract) — informative |
 
 Gap this proposal fills: a **spec index + consolidated property-key registry**
 and a **cross-language validator** so the split files read as one implementable
 whole and cannot drift.
 
 ## 5. Scope & work packages (core-first, Java + SSR first)
 
 The **core is the deliverable** (an implementable open standard); the visual
 layer is cheap proof, not the product.
 
 **Deliberately narrow first scope.** Cross-platform and polyglot deliverables

 (HTML first paint + delta updates over WebSocket) — the flagship path that
 directly addresses enterprise Java teams. The core deliverable is the open
 **standard layer** (spec, registry, conformance, validator). No scope-creep into
 additional DSLs or renderers in this grant; embedded/native/mobile surfaces are
 future phases.

 (submitted with the proposal). WP5 adds the **WCAG/ARIA compliance pass** and the
