 ## 8. Prior-art comparison
 
 Airbnb, Lyft and Spotify ship proprietary, per-app SDUI JSON schemas — closed,
 not an open standard. Flutter, React Native and Compose Multiplatform are
 frameworks that couple the UI model to one runtime. Native toolkits (GTK,
 SwiftUI, WinUI) are per-platform and closed. Generic serialization (JSON,
 Protobuf) is schema-driven data transport, not a UI instruction stream, and
 re-sends full trees. Pathland is a **16-byte command stream** (tree mutations +
 properties), open-spec, process/transport-agnostic, with native-element renderers
 and zero-copy, diff-based emission — an open standard, not another framework.
 
 The structural difference: a framework cannot escape its runtime. A protocol
 lets any language drive any renderer, which is what enables, for example, a
 **composition proxy** that combines several backend applications toward one
 renderer — a materially better answer to microfrontends than today's
 BFF/frontend-app stacks.
 
 ## 9. European dimension & ecosystem
 
 - **Digital sovereignty**: an open, Apache-2.0 UI protocol reduces dependence on
   non-European UI stacks — a "made in Europe" contribution to the Open Internet
   Stack's *independent and cross-platform development framework* area. Open
   standards let all companies participate, rather than a few foreign vendors.
 - **Open standards / interoperability**: spec + conformance vectors let any
   vendor implement renderers/DSLs; the validator and conformance suite become a
   reusable tool for any SDUI adopter.
 - **Efficiency/frugality**: 16-byte opcodes + zero-delta emission cut bandwidth
   and embedded power vs JSON SDUI.
 - **Engagement**: the first concrete adopter is **internal** (SOS International,
   where Lumen is in production). Near-term, the applicant aims to present the
   protocol at **WebDevCon** (if accepted) and is considering **FOSDEM** (free,
   volunteer-run) as an open-source venue. Embedded outreach is deferred until
   embedded enters the roadmap in a later phase.

 All software FOSS (Apache-2.0); all open outcomes open access. Deliverables are
 **WCAG-compliant** where they include web surfaces (this is an explicit

   demo modules, hosted demo URL, screenshots
 - [ ] NLnet final report + MoU deliverables (PM)
 
 ## 12. Two-page narrative (copy-ready for the NLnet form)
 
 **Proposal name:** Pathland — an implementable open UI-protocol standard.
 
 **What it is.** Pathland is an open, Apache-2.0 protocol for declarative,
 retained-mode UI that is language- and platform-agnostic. It describes *what* a
 UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment — as a stream of fixed
 **16-byte opcodes**, never *where*. Emission is diff-based and reactive: only the
 nodes that changed emit, an unchanged tree emits zero opcodes, and renderers are
 pure functions of the stream that map onto native elements. The engine is
 transport- and process-agnostic, running from embedded to in-browser WASM to
 distributed server-driven backends. The spec already exists (split across
 `spec/OPCODE`, `PRIMITIVES`, `MODIFIERS`, `EVENTS`, `CONFORMANCE`, plus the `DSL`
 authoring surface) and is enforced by golden byte vectors.
 
 **What we will build.** This project turns the working proof-of-concept into an
 **implementable open standard**: (1) a spec index and consolidated property-key
 registry; (2) a machine-readable ID schema and cross-language validator so the
 language surfaces cannot drift; (3) coverage-guided fuzzing and a Miri pass
 proving the decoders and the C ABI are robust against malformed input — the
 baseline for an independent security audit; (4) a benchmark suite quantifying
 the 16-byte-vs-JSON/Protobuf and vs-htmx/BFF claims; and (5) **WCAG/ARIA
 compliance on the HTML renderer** and the evidence pack (CI, a hosted SSR HTML
 demo, and screenshots already exist as application evidence). A solo maintainer
 delivers this in six months at 260 hours (cost-recovery, €11,700).
 
 **Why it matters.** An open UI *protocol* — rather than another UI *framework* —
 lets any vendor build renderers and DSLs against one spec, reducing lock-in to
 non-European stacks and supporting the Open Internet Stack's cross-platform
 development goal. The 16-byte, zero-delta wire format is an efficiency answer to
 bloated JSON SDUI. Prior art (Airbnb/Lyft/Spotify SDUI, Flutter, React Native)
 is closed or runtime-coupled; nothing provides an open, diff-based binary
 instruction stream across embedded, browser, desktop, and server.
 
 **European dimension.** Made in Denmark; Apache-2.0; the standard and conformance
 suite become a reusable tool for any EU SDUI adopter, reducing dependence on
 foreign UI stacks.
 
 ## 13. Human contribution & Generative AI
 
 Pathland's design is human-directed. The applicant made the architectural

 ## Goal
 
 A cross-platform router for Pathland: browser-path parity (Angular Router /
 react-router style) **and** native navigation compatibility (SwiftUI
 NavigationStack, Jetpack Compose NavHost, WinUI NavigationView, LVGL screens),
 built as a DSL-level construct that respects the protocol's non-negotiables:
 stateless renderers, app-owned tree, diff-based emission, "WHAT never WHERE".
 
 ## Foundation-first design
 
 **Conditional rendering (structural reactivity) is the reusable primitive.**
 A structural container owns a subtree selected by a signal and reconciles it on
 change, emitting `TREE` deltas. The router is a structural container whose
 content function is route-table matching, plus router-specific extras
 (back-stack, URL sync, the `NAVIGATE` event, the `ROUTE`/`TRANSITION`
 properties).
 
 ## Locked decisions
 
 | Decision | Choice |
 |---|---|
 | Foundation | Conditional rendering **first** (shared subtree-swap machinery); router built on it |
 | Conditional DSL surface (Java) | `Conditional.when(...)` + `Case.of(...)` / `Case.otherwise(...)`, statically importable — mirrors `Signals` (final class, private ctor, lowercase factories) |
 | Container | Group-backed slot (bare `VSTACK` node, `Group.java`), not ZStack |
 | Protocol surface (router only) | `ROUTE` property, `TRANSITION` hint, `NAVIGATE` event — conditional rendering adds **zero** wire surface |
 | State ownership | App owns state; web mirrors history (`popstate` → `NAVIGATE` back to app) |
 | Spec ordering | `spec/DSL.md` first (structural-reactivity exception + router), then wire specs |
 | Languages | Java + Rust in parallel |
 | Event name | `NAVIGATE` (`0x0E`, subsumes back/forward/popstate/deep-link) |
 | v1 URL sync | Always `pushState`; `replaceState` for `replace()` = documented follow-up |
 
 ## Java conditional API
 
 ```java
 import static dev.pathland.view.Conditional.when;
 import static dev.pathland.view.Conditional.Case;
 
 when(showLogin, LoginView.of(), HomeView.of());                 // if / else
 when(mode, Case.of(HOME, HomeView.of()),
           Case.of(USERS, UsersView.of()),
           Case.otherwise(NotFoundView.of()));                   // switch + default
 ```
 
 (`if`/`switch`/`case`/`else` are Java keywords — `when` is Kotlin's `switch`
 analog and a valid Java identifier.)
 
 ## Architecture
 
 1. **Structural container (Java emitter):** owns a subtree selected by a
    signal; on change, rebuilds content and **reconciles** against the retained
    `PathlandNode` snapshot, emitting `TREE` deltas; identical structure → zero
    opcodes.
 2. **RouterCore (DSL):** `Router` (`Signal<Route>` + back-stack,
    `navigate/push/pop/replace/back`), `Route`, `RouteTable`, `NavigationContainer`
    (structural container + `ROUTE`/`TRANSITION`), `NavigationLink`, `Location`
    (`Browser`/`InMemory`).
 3. **Protocol hooks:** `ROUTE` (URL sync in-stream), `TRANSITION` (native-feel
    transitions), `NAVIGATE` (platform back/gesture → app).
 
 ## Native compatibility
 
 SwiftUI `NavigationStack` / Compose `NavHost` → slot + child swap +
 `TRANSITION`, back → `NAVIGATE` → `pop()`; WinUI `NavigationView` → `HStack`
 sidebar+detail, per-outlet slots; LVGL screens → whole-tree swap (app's
 back-stack supplies the stack LVGL lacks). A slot carrying `ROUTE` is a
 navigation slot and **may** be promoted onto the platform's native navigation
 container; the renderer keeps the back-stack app-owned and only maps child
 swaps → native push/pop, `ROUTE` → native path, `TRANSITION` → native
 transition, and native back affordances → `NAVIGATE`. See `spec/DSL.md §4.5`.

 ### Fix (post-Phase-6): SPA catch-all no longer shadows `/ws`
 
 The deep-link catch-all initially matched `/ws`, so the WebSocket handshake was
 answered with HTML 200 instead of a 101 upgrade — clicks went nowhere. Fixed:
 Spring `IndexController` `@GetMapping(value = "/{*path}", headers = "!Upgrade")`
 (WebSocket upgrades carry `Upgrade: websocket` and bypass the catch-all to reach
 the registered handler); Quarkus `IndexResource` `@Path("{path:(?!ws).*}")`
 (negative lookahead excludes the literal `ws` path). Verified headlessly: a
 WebSocket client gets a **101** handshake, and a synthetic tap on a link id makes
 the server reply with `ROUTE "/users"` + the destination swap — in both demos.

+package dev.pathland.demo.ad
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.Color as JColor
+import dev.pathland.view.core.FontWeight
+import dev.pathland.view.core.HorizontalAlignment

+
+/**
+ * A small self-contained demo app — a title and a button that reacts to clicks —
+ * used as the **origin** of the music player's sponsored proxy slot
+ * (spec/PROXY.md).
+ *
+ * It is mounted as its own Pathland app (e.g. `/ad` on the same server) and
+ * embedded into the player's Now Playing pane via a `ProxyView`. Clicking the
+ * button updates this app's own per-session state; the delta is forwarded
+ * through the proxy and applied in place — the embedded app is fully
+ * interactive.
+ *
+ * A Java host mounts it with `new AdView()` or `AdView.make()`.
+ */
+class AdView : KotlinView() {
+
+    /** The per-session click count (persisted under an explicit store key). */
+    private var clicks by state(0, "ad.clicks")
+
+    override fun body(): View =
+        VStack(alignment = HorizontalAlignment.CENTER, spacing = 10f) {
+            Text("Pathland Ads")
+                .fontSize(16f)
+                .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)
+            Text("A second app, served on this same server, embedded here via a proxy view.")
+                .fontSize(12f)
+                .foregroundStyle(JColor.rgb(0x4B, 0x55, 0x63))
+            Button("Click me") { clicks += 1 }
+            Text(computed {
+                if (clicks == 1) "Clicked 1 time" else "Clicked $clicks times"
+            }).fontSize(13f).fontWeight(FontWeight.SEMIBOLD)
+        }
+            .padding(16f)
+            .background(JColor.rgb(0xE8, 0xEF, 0xFF))
+            .cornerRadius(10f)
+
+    companion object {
+        /** Java-compatible factory. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun make(): AdView = AdView()
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.demo.ad
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.Environment
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Categories
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Commands
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Components
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Opcode
+import dev.pathland.view.core.state.InMemoryStateStore
+import dev.pathland.view.core.state.PersistentState
+import dev.pathland.view.core.transport.FrameOpcodeSink
+import dev.pathland.view.core.transport.ProtocolFrame
+import dev.pathland.view.engine.Emitter
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertTrue
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
+
+/**
+ * The small ad app — a title and a button that reacts to clicks — the origin of
+ * the music player's sponsored proxy slot (spec/PROXY.md).
+ */
+class AdViewTest {
+
+    @Test
+    fun buttonClickIncrementsTheCounter() {
+        val state = PersistentState(InMemoryStateStore(), "session-1")
+        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
+        val result = Emitter(sink).mount(AdView(), Environment(state))
+
+        assertTrue(anySetText(sink.frame(), "Pathland Ads"), "the title renders")
+        assertTrue(anySetText(sink.frame(), "Clicked 0 times"), "the counter starts at zero")
+
+        val buttonId = sink.frame().opcodes().stream()
+            .filter { it.category() == Categories.TREE && it.command() == Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE }
+            .filter { (it.b() and 0xFFFF) == Components.BUTTON }
+            .mapToInt { it.a() }
+            .findFirst()
+            .orElseThrow { AssertionError("no button node") }
+
+        // The host routes a tap into its action; the action writes the counter
+        // state, and the emitter re-emits only its text.
+        result.tapActions()[buttonId]!!.run()
+
+        assertTrue(anySetText(sink.frame(), "Clicked 1 time"), "the click increments the counter")
+    }
+
+    private fun anySetText(frame: ProtocolFrame, text: String): Boolean =
+        frame.opcodes().any {
+            it.category() == Categories.PARAMETER &&
+                it.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_TEXT &&
+                text == frame.stringAt(it.b())
+        }
+}

-# pathland-demo-views — implementation status
-
-**Last updated:** November 3, 2026
-
-The remaining framework-agnostic **Java** demo views (`dev.pathland.demo`), consumed
-by the Quarkus and Spring Boot demos. Uses `State` fields wired by the
-`pathland-view-processor` annotation processor.
-
-The music player moved to `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`; the shared demo theme and
-assets moved to the DSL-neutral `pathland-demo-common` module.
-
-## Implemented
-
-- **`KitchenSinkView`** — a scrollable column of every protocol section.
-- **Sections** — `SectionCard`, `CounterSection`, `TextFieldSection`,
-  `ToggleSection`, `ValueControlsSection`, `PickerSection`, `ColorSection`,
-  `DateSection`, `LayoutSection`, `TextStylesSection`, `AppearanceSection`, and
-  `ThemeSection`.
-- **Legacy views** — `CounterView`, `CounterControls`, `NameField`.
-- **`SplitNavDemo`** — sidebar + detail navigation with `NavigationContainer`,
-  route-driven window metadata, reactive active-row highlighting, and a fallback.
-- **`AdView`** — the small sponsored-proxy origin app.
-- **Semantic accessibility** — `MAIN`/`NAVIGATION`/`HEADER` roles; sidebar rows
-  are real `Button`s; controls carry accessible labels.
-- **Real asset refs** — icons use the semantic `Icon` primitive; non-icon media
-  assets live in `pathland-demo-common`.
-- **`DemoTheme` and `DemoAssets`** — now provided by `pathland-demo-common`.
-
-## Not implemented / gaps
-
-- The browser experience depends on the `@pathland/dom-renderer` client.
-- These Java views remain a pre-1.0 porting target for Kotlin (#169).
-
-## Verified by
-
-`mvn test -pl pathland-demo-views` (JDK 17+) — `CounterViewTest`,
-`KitchenSinkViewTest`, and `SplitNavDemoTest`.

 # pathland-quarkus-kotlin-demo — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 1, 2026
 
 Kotlin-first Quarkus demo: SSR plus live 16-byte opcode deltas over WebSocket,
 authored with `pathland-view-kotlin` and hosted by `pathland-quarkus-kotlin`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - Kotlin `PathlandApp` CDI bean (`KotlinDemoApplication`) and a Kotlin-owned
   `KotlinView` root (`KotlinDemoView`).
 - Exercises persisted state (`count`, `items`), two-way text input (`name`),
   reactive computed text, `ForEach`, and Kotlin modifier sugar.
 - Quarkus Kotlin build setup: `kotlin-maven-plugin`, `all-open` for CDI/JAX-RS
   annotations, `jvmTarget=17`.
-- Maven Enforcer bans `pathland-view` and `pathland-demo-views`: the demo is
+- The removed Java DSL (`pathland-view`) and Java demo views are not on the
+  classpath: the demo is
   Kotlin-DSL-only.
 - `KotlinDemoSmokeTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts the CDI bean is discovered, SSR
   renders the Kotlin tree, and the SSR document references the content-hashed DOM
   bundle (a GET on that URL returns 200).
 - The DOM renderer bundle + service worker are copied by
   `lib/typescript/scripts/copy-to-demos.mjs`.
 - Run with `scripts/run-quarkus-kotlin-demo.sh` → `http://localhost:8080`.

 # pathland-quarkus — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 1, 2026
 
 DSL-neutral Quarkus extension for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
 app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding this extension + a
 `PathlandApp` CDI bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at
-their own subpaths (the BFF layout). Author the root view with `pathland-view`
-(Java DSL extension) or `pathland-view-kotlin` (Kotlin DSL extension).
+their own subpaths (the BFF layout). Author the root view with
+`pathland-view-kotlin`; Java hosts return Kotlin views from a `PathlandApp` bean.
 
 ## Implemented
 
+- **Java host / Kotlin views**: `CounterApp` is a Java CDI bean whose
+  `newRoot()` returns a Kotlin-authored fixture view; the multi-session
+  WebSocket tests prove SSR + live deltas work through that mount.
+
 - **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
 
 - **`PathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/_pathland/ws")` for the root app: 1:1 sessions
   per connection (a fresh `uiId` per connection + the client's `wid` state scope from
   the `?wid=` query param), binary events routed into the root registry of the
   `PathlandHost`. **Stateless (critical)**: quarkus-websockets-next endpoints default
   to `@Singleton` — one shared instance for all connections — so the per-connection
   ids come from `connection.id()` + the handshake and the `QuarkusConnection` adapters
   live in a map keyed by connection id. Memoizing `uiId`/`wid`/`transport` on the
   shared instance collapsed every connection onto ONE session (multiple browsers shared
   one UI model — a probe or second tab drove the first tab's session).
 - **`MountedPathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/{app}/_pathland/ws")` for mounted apps:
   the `{app}` path param resolves the app's registry. Mount paths are single-segment.
   Same stateless rule as the root socket.
 - **`IndexResource`** — JAX-RS SSR catch-all (`/` + deep links; `/_pathland/**` and the
   Quarkus non-application root `/q/**` — health/metrics — excluded via negative lookahead)
   dispatching to the longest-mount app (prefix stripped);
   SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS);
   per-app framework files (`/{app}/_pathland/...`, e.g. the mounted app's bundle) are
   served from the shared `/_pathland/**` classpath mount. Quarkus serves the global
   `/_pathland/**` bundle + asset mount from `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS.
   **`/_pathland/{name}.css`** (global JAX-RS route + the mounted-base
   `frameworkFile` path) serves the renderer-owned content-hashed base design
   (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
   `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. **`/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg`**
   serves the renderer-owned icon glyphs from the shared Rust renderer
   (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache
   header — no static CSS/icon files on any host. SSR links the CSS via
   `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
 - **`PathlandRegistryProducer`** — CDI `@Produces @Singleton` `PathlandHost` from every
   `MountedApp` bean plus the lone `PathlandApp` bean (mounted at `/`); `@Disposes` shuts
   it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable
   per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`)
   to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at
   `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
 - **`ServiceWorkerFilter`** — serves `/_pathland/sw.js` (root and mounted bases) with
   `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the client's root-scoped
   registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over
   Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured
   max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection).
 - **Observability (issue #62)** — `quarkus-micrometer` (a `MeterRegistry` bean) +
   `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the
   registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and
   `quarkus.otel.enabled` (default `true`; the extension never touches the OTel API when
   the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the
   host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear
   at `/q/metrics`.
 - **`QuarkusConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketConnection` to `PathlandConnection`.
   Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued),
   and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM
   client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an
   "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a
   `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection /
   a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would
   otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection
   sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm
   through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive
   scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it).
 - **Heartbeat** — both sockets reply to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
   **at the transport layer** (through their `QuarkusConnection`, no actor/session
   dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md
   §Transport heartbeat.
 - **Failure handling** — `fail()` logs the reason; `close()` (socket `@OnClose`)
   no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious
   "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection
   that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel
   (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is
   **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't
   false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly
   (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed).
 - `META-INF/beans.xml` so Quarkus discovers the extension.
 - **Quarkus extension metadata** — runtime + `pathland-quarkus-deployment`; the
   runtime provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus` capability. The runtime has no
-  dependency on either authoring DSL (`pathland-view` / `pathland-view-kotlin`).
+  dependency on the authoring DSL. Tests use Kotlin-authored fixture views to prove
+  a Java CDI bean can mount them.

 ```java
 @ApplicationScoped
 public class MyApp {
     @Produces @Singleton PathlandApp main() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
     @Produces @Singleton MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); }

 Playing pane embeds the small `/ad` app via a **same-server `ProxyView`**,

 sessions** against `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar
 probe) and asserts each connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated,
 and is never closed by the peer.
 `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts `/q/health` reports the Pathland
 check UP and `/q/metrics` exposes the `pathland.*` namespace. `BaseCssTest`

                                 </condition>

                                      this copies each into META-INF/native/<os>-<arch>/.

                                      embeds the host Rust debug build in the flat
                                      META-INF/native/ layout. -->
                                 <property name="pathland.native.staging" value="${project.basedir}/target/native" />
                                 <available file="${pathland.native.staging}" type="dir" property="pathland.native.staged" />
                                 <property name="pathland.native.host" value="${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html${pathland.native.ext}" />
                                 <available file="${pathland.native.host}" property="pathland.native.host.present" />

                                         <and>
                                             <not><isset property="pathland.native.staged" /></not>
                                             <not><isset property="pathland.native.host.present" /></not>
                                         </and>
                                     </condition>
                                 </fail>

 # pathland-spring-boot-starter — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** October 28, 2026
 
 Spring Boot auto-configuration for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
 app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding the starter dependency + a
 `PathlandApp` bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own
 subpaths (the BFF layout).
 
 ## Implemented
 
+- **Java host / Kotlin views**: `KotlinViewMountTest` proves a Java-only
+  `@SpringBootApplication` bean returning `PathlandApp` mounts a Kotlin-authored
+  fixture view, renders it through SSR, and receives a live signal delta.
+
 - **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
 
 - **`PathlandAutoConfiguration`** (`@AutoConfiguration`, `@EnableWebSocket` since Spring
   Boot 3.5 no longer auto-enables it) + `META-INF/spring/…/AutoConfiguration.imports`:
   - default `StateStore` bean (`@ConditionalOnMissingBean` — Redis-or-in-memory),
   - `PathlandHost` bean (shut down with the context): every `MountedApp` bean plus the
     lone `PathlandApp` bean mounted at `/` (unless an explicit `MountedApp` claims the
     root). Without any app the host is empty and the starter is inert.
   - a `WebSocketConfigurer` registering **one handler per app** at its framework base
     (`/_pathland/ws` for the root, `/{mount}/_pathland/ws` otherwise). Each connection
     gets a fresh `uiId` (its UI model) + the client's `wid` (per-window state scope)
     from the WS `?wid=` query param (kept in `sessionStorage`, never in the page URL),
   - `PathlandIndexController` (SSR catch-all dispatching to the longest-mount app with
     the prefix stripped + a framework static controller serving the bundle + asset mount
     from `classpath:/static/_pathland/**` at both `/_pathland/**` and `/{app}/_pathland/**`;
     the more-specific mapping beats `/{*path}`, and the `!Upgrade` header excludes WS).
     When no static file matches, the controller serves renderer-owned assets from the
     shared Rust renderer: the content-hashed base stylesheet
     (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
     `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and
     `/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg` glyphs (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` →
     `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache header — no static CSS/icon
     files on any host, and a host can still override either with a file. SSR links
     the CSS via `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
     The framework controller honors byte-range requests (`206 Partial Content` +
     `Content-Range`, `416` for unsatisfiable ranges, `Accept-Ranges` on the full
     response) — a `<video>` (a `MediaController`'s playback) seeking beyond its
     buffer issues a `Range`
     request, and answering it with a full `200` would make browsers restart the media
     at byte 0.
     SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS).
 - **SSR debug comments**: the host reads the `pathland.debug-html` property
   (`@Value("${pathland.debug-html:false}")`) and forwards it to each registry, enabling
   per-node HTML comments in SSR output when set.
 - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `pathland.service-worker`
   (default `false`) forwards to the host; the SSR emits `data-pathland-service-worker`
   and the controller serves `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` +
   `Cache-Control: no-cache` (a stable, uncached script the browser byte-compares).
 - **`SpringConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketSession` to `PathlandConnection`.
   `AutoCloseable`: a failed send surfaces as a close (the session's
   `closeConnection` closes the underlying session) so the DOM client reconnects +
   `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an open socket.
 - **Heartbeat** — the socket replies to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
   **at the transport layer** (through its `SpringConnection`, no actor/session
   dependency; spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat).
 - **Observability (issue #62)** — `spring-boot-starter-actuator` supplies the
   `MeterRegistry`; auto-config builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over it (decorated with
   `TracingTelemetry` when an `OpenTelemetry` bean is present — add
   `micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel` to opt in) and a `HealthIndicator` reporting the host
   UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/actuator/health`. The `pathland.*` meters are
   exposed at `/actuator/prometheus` (add `micrometer-registry-prometheus`).
 
 ## App DX
 
 ```java
 @SpringBootApplication
 public class MyApp {
     public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(MyApp.class, args); }
     @Bean PathlandApp pathlandApp() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
     @Bean MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); } // optional 2nd app
 }
 ```
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `mvn test` — `PathlandAutoConfigurationTest` (`@SpringBootTest`): a `PathlandApp` bean
 mounts at `/` and SSR renders the root. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest`
 (`@SpringBootTest(RANDOM_PORT)`) opens **100 concurrent real WS sessions** against
 `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar probe) and asserts each
 connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated, and is never closed by
 the peer. `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts
 `/actuator/health` reports the `pathland` component UP and the auto-configured
 `PathlandTelemetry` is a `MicrometerTelemetry` registering `pathland.*` meters.
 `BaseCssHeadersTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts the linked SSR
 `<link>`, the immutable `text/css` response at the global and mounted bases, and
 a 404 for an unknown hash.
 Manual: the `pathland-spring-boot-demo` renders `/`, `/kitchen`, `/settings`
 and the 404 fallback **and a second app at `/app2`**; a WebSocket handshake to
 `/_pathland/ws` and `/app2/_pathland/ws` returns 101.

          xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
          xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
     <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>
 
     <parent>
         <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
         <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
         <version>0.1.5</version>
     </parent>
 
     <artifactId>pathland-view-core</artifactId>
     <packaging>jar</packaging>
 
     <name>Pathland View Core</name>
     <description>
-        Framework-agnostic Pathland JVM engine and runtime: the 16-byte opcode protocol
-        (dev.pathland.view.core.protocol), retained-tree diff emitter
-        (dev.pathland.view.engine), Angular-style signals, wire codec, router, state, and
-        lazy JNA ring interop. Shared by the Java and Kotlin authoring DSLs and by server
-        runtimes. Runs on every LTS from Java 17; JNA is the only runtime dependency.
+        Framework-agnostic Pathland JVM engine and runtime, written in Kotlin: the
+        16-byte opcode protocol, retained-tree diff emitter, Angular-style signals,
+        wire codec, router, state, and lazy JNA ring interop. The Kotlin DSL and all
+        server runtimes depend on this module. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.
     </description>
 
     <dependencies>
         <dependency>
+            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
+            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
+            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
+        </dependency>
+        <dependency>
             <groupId>net.java.dev.jna</groupId>
             <artifactId>jna</artifactId>
         </dependency>
         <dependency>
             <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
             <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
             <scope>test</scope>
         </dependency>
     </dependencies>
 
     <build>
         <plugins>
             <plugin>
+                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
+                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
+                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
+                <executions>
+                    <execution>
+                        <id>compile</id>
+                        <phase>process-sources</phase>
+                        <goals>
+                            <goal>compile</goal>
+                        </goals>
+                        <configuration>
+                            <sourceDirs>
+                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</sourceDir>
+                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/main/java</sourceDir>
+                            </sourceDirs>
+                        </configuration>
+                    </execution>
+                    <execution>
+                        <id>test-compile</id>
+                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
+                        <goals>
+                            <goal>test-compile</goal>
+                        </goals>
+                        <configuration>
+                            <sourceDirs>
+                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
+                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/java</sourceDir>
+                            </sourceDirs>
+                        </configuration>
+                    </execution>
+                </executions>
+                <configuration>
+                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
+                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
+                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
+                    <args>
+                        <arg>-Xjvm-default=all</arg>
+                    </args>
+                </configuration>
+            </plugin>
+            <plugin>
                 <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                 <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                 <configuration>
                     <!-- Point the test JVM at the Rust cdylib for JNA ring tests.
                          Absent the dylib, those tests are skipped via an assumption. -->
                     <argLine>-Djava.library.path=${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug</argLine>
                 </configuration>
             </plugin>
         </plugins>
     </build>
 </project>

+package dev.pathland.view.core

+/** An adaptive theme: a light and a dark Theme pair. */
+class AdaptiveTheme(
+    private val light: Theme,
+    private val dark: Theme,
+) : ThemeData {
+    fun light(): Theme = light
+    fun dark(): Theme = dark
+
+    override fun emitInto(sink: OpcodeSink) {
+        light.emitInto(sink)
+        for (o in dark.overrides()) {
+            sink.setDesignToken(dark(o.path), o.valueType, o.value)
+        }

+    private fun dark(path: String): String =

+object Configurators {

+    fun <V, C> view(

+        setter: Consumer<C>,
+    ): ViewBuilder<V, C> where V : View, V : Configurable<C>, C : View.Config {

+
+/** The rendering environment — the single inheritance/scoping mechanism. */
+class Environment(private val state: PersistentState?) {
+
+    private var windowMetadata: WindowMetadata? = null
+
+    /** The window/surface metadata declared by the root, or null. */
+    fun windowMetadata(): WindowMetadata? = windowMetadata
+
+    /** Record the root-declared window metadata during its render. */
+    internal fun setWindowMetadata(metadata: WindowMetadata?) {
+        windowMetadata = metadata
+    }
+
+    /** The session's persistent state (null for a stateless environment). */
+    fun state(): PersistentState? = state
+
+    companion object {
+        @JvmField
+        val BUTTON_STYLE: EnvironmentKey<ButtonStyle> = EnvironmentKey.of("buttonStyle")
+
+        @JvmField
+        val LABEL_STYLE: EnvironmentKey<LabelStyle> = EnvironmentKey.of("labelStyle")
+
+        @JvmField
+        val VIDEO_STYLE: EnvironmentKey<VideoStyle> = EnvironmentKey.of("videoStyle")
+
+        private val VALUES: ThreadLocal<EnvironmentValues> =
+            ThreadLocal.withInitial { EnvironmentValues.empty() }
+
+        /** The default environment (no persistent state). */
+        @JvmField
+        val DEFAULT = Environment(null)
+
+        /** The current scope (empty at the top of a render). */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun current(): EnvironmentValues = VALUES.get()
+
+        /** The scoped value for [key] as a signal (reactive). */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun <T> value(key: EnvironmentKey<T>): Signal<T> {
+            val scope = VALUES.get()
+            if (scope.contains(key)) {
+                return toSignal(scope.get(key))
+            }
+            return EnvironmentSignal(key)
+        }
+
+        @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
+        private fun <T> toSignal(value: Any?): Signal<T> {
+            if (value is Signal<*>) return value as Signal<T>
+            return Signal { value as T }
+        }
+
+        private class EnvironmentSignal<T>(private val key: EnvironmentKey<T>) : Signal<T> {
+            private var captured: Signal<T>? = null
+
+            @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
+            override fun get(): T {
+                val scope = VALUES.get()
+                if (scope.contains(key)) {
+                    captured = toSignal(scope.get(key))
+                }
+                return captured?.get() as T
+            }
+        }
+
+        /** Temporarily set the active scope for a render. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun within(scope: EnvironmentValues) {
+            VALUES.set(scope)
+        }
+
+        /** Restore the previous active scope. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun restore(previous: EnvironmentValues) {
+            VALUES.set(previous)
+        }
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core
+
+import java.util.HashMap
+
+/** An immutable, hierarchical scope of environment values. */
+class EnvironmentValues private constructor(
+    private val parent: EnvironmentValues?,
+    private val key: EnvironmentKey<*>?,
+    private val value: Any?,
+) {
+    /** A scope extending this one with a binding (nearest wins). */
+    fun <T> with(key: EnvironmentKey<T>, value: T): EnvironmentValues =
+        EnvironmentValues(this, key, value)
+
+    /** The value bound to [key], walking the chain; null when absent. */
+    @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
+    fun <T> get(key: EnvironmentKey<T>): T? {
+        var node: EnvironmentValues? = this
+        while (node != null) {
+            if (node.key === key) return node.value as T?
+            node = node.parent
+        }
+        return null
+    }
+
+    /** Whether [key] is bound anywhere in the chain. */
+    fun contains(key: EnvironmentKey<*>): Boolean {
+        var node: EnvironmentValues? = this
+        while (node != null) {
+            if (node.key === key) return true
+            node = node.parent
+        }
+        return false
+    }
+
+    internal fun flattened(): Map<EnvironmentKey<*>, Any?> {
+        val out = HashMap<EnvironmentKey<*>, Any?>()
+        var node: EnvironmentValues? = this
+        while (node != null) {
+            if (node.key != null && !out.containsKey(node.key)) {
+                out[node.key] = node.value
+            }
+            node = node.parent
+        }
+        return out
+    }
+
+    override fun equals(other: Any?): Boolean =
+        other is EnvironmentValues && flattened() == other.flattened()
+
+    override fun hashCode(): Int = flattened().hashCode()
+
+    companion object {
+        private val EMPTY = EnvironmentValues(null, null, null)
+
+        /** The empty scope (no bindings). */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun empty(): EnvironmentValues = EMPTY
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signal
+import dev.pathland.view.engine.PathlandNode
+import dev.pathland.view.engine.ReactiveValues
+
+/** A view wrapped by property modifiers or a custom ViewModifier. */
+class Modified private constructor(
+    private val inner: View,
+    private val props: List<Prop>,
+    private val modifier: ViewModifier?,
+) : View {
+
+    /** One property application: a static value or a reactive signal. */
+    data class Prop(
+        val property: Int,
+        val value: Any?,
+        val signal: Signal<*>?,
+    ) {
+        fun property(): Int = property
+        fun value(): Any? = value
+        fun signal(): Signal<*>? = signal
+
+        companion object {
+            @JvmStatic
+            fun value(property: Int, value: Any?): Prop = Prop(property, value, null)
+
+            @JvmStatic
+            fun reactive(property: Int, signal: Signal<*>): Prop = Prop(property, null, signal)
+        }
+    }
+
+    /** The wrapped view (the next link inward in this modifier chain). */
+    fun inner(): View = inner
+
+    override fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
+        if (modifier != null) {
+            return modifier.body(inner).renderNode(env)
+        }
+        val node = inner.renderNode(env)
+        for (p in props) {
+            if (p.signal != null) {
+                val value = ReactiveValues.initial(p.property, p.signal)
+                node.properties[p.property] = value
+                node.propertyBindings[p.property] = p.signal
+            } else {
+                node.properties[p.property] = p.value
+            }
+        }
+        return node
+    }
+
+    companion object {
+        /** A static property mod. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun prop(property: Int, value: Any?): Prop = Prop.value(property, value)
+
+        /** A reactive property mod. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun prop(property: Int, signal: Signal<*>): Prop = Prop.reactive(property, signal)
+
+        /** Build a property-modifier view from inner + props. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun props(inner: View, vararg props: Prop): Modified = Modified(inner, props.toList(), null)
+
+        /** A custom-view-modifier wrapper. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun apply(inner: View, modifier: ViewModifier): Modified = Modified(inner, emptyList(), modifier)
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Commands
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Properties
+import dev.pathland.view.engine.PathlandNode
+
+/** A view wrapped by `onTapGesture`: declares pointer listeners and records the action. */
+internal class TapGestureView(private val content: View, private val action: Runnable?) : View {
+    override fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
+        val node = content.renderNode(env)
+        val existing = node.properties[Properties.EVENT_LISTENERS]
+        val mask = if (existing is Int) existing else 0
+        node.properties[Properties.EVENT_LISTENERS] =
+            mask or Commands.Listeners.POINTER_DOWN or Commands.Listeners.POINTER_UP
+        if (action != null) node.tapActions.add(action)
+        return node
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.ValueTypes
+import dev.pathland.view.core.transport.OpcodeSink
+
+/** A batch of global design-token overrides for a single scheme. */
+class Theme : ThemeData {
+
+    /** A single token override (path, wire value type, typed value). */
+    data class TokenOverride(
+        val path: String,
+        val valueType: Int,
+        val value: Any,
+    ) {
+        fun path(): String = path
+        fun valueType(): Int = valueType
+        fun value(): Any = value
+    }
+
+    private val overrides = ArrayList<TokenOverride>()
+
+    fun color(path: String, argb: Int): Theme = push(path, ValueTypes.COLOR, Color.of(argb))
+    fun f32(path: String, value: Float): Theme = push(path, ValueTypes.F32, value)
+    fun u32(path: String, value: Int): Theme = push(path, ValueTypes.U32, value)
+    fun u8(path: String, value: Int): Theme = push(path, ValueTypes.U8, value)
+    fun string(path: String, value: String): Theme = push(path, ValueTypes.STRING, value)
+
+    private fun push(path: String, valueType: Int, value: Any): Theme {
+        overrides.add(TokenOverride(path, valueType, value))
+        return this
+    }
+
+    internal fun overrides(): List<TokenOverride> = overrides
+
+    override fun emitInto(sink: OpcodeSink) {
+        for (o in overrides) {
+            sink.setDesignToken(o.path, o.valueType, o.value)
+        }
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core
+
+import dev.pathland.view.engine.Emitter
+import dev.pathland.view.engine.PathlandNode
+import java.util.Objects
+import java.util.function.Supplier
+
+/**
+ * A composable view. Composite views declare their subtree with [body]; primitives
+ * override [renderNode] to materialize a [PathlandNode].
+ */
+interface View {
+    /** The base marker for a view's value config. */
+    interface Config
+
+    /** Declarative composition: a composite view returns its subtree here. */
+    fun body(): View = this
+
+    /** The emitter entry point: render this view as a tracked component slot. */
+    fun render(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
+        val emitter = Emitter.current()
+        return if (emitter == null) renderNode(env) else emitter.renderView(this, env)
+    }
+
+    /** The root-chain render. */
+    fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
+        val resolved = body()
+        if (resolved !== this) {
+            return resolved.renderNode(env)
+        }
+        throw UnsupportedOperationException(
+            javaClass.name + " must override body() (composite) or renderNode() (primitive)",
+        )
+    }
+
+    /** Wrap this view in modifiers, applied innermost-first. */
+    fun modifiers(vararg modifiers: ViewModifier): View {
+        var result: View = this
+        for (modifier in modifiers) {
+            result = Modified.apply(result, modifier)
+        }
+        return result
+    }
+
+    companion object {
+        /** A reactive subtree from a supplier: the inline form of control flow. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun of(content: Supplier<View>): View =
+            ReactiveSlotView(Objects.requireNonNull(content, "content"))
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core
+
+import dev.pathland.view.engine.PathlandNode
+import java.util.ArrayList
+
+/** The chainable result of a view's static `make(...)` entry point. */
+class ViewBuilder<V, C>(
+    private val view: V,
+) : View where V : View, V : Configurable<C>, C : View.Config {
+
+    private val modifiers = ArrayList<ViewModifier>()
+    private val children = ArrayList<View>()
+
+    /** Apply modifiers (innermost-first). */
+    override fun modifiers(vararg modifiers: ViewModifier): ViewBuilder<V, C> {
+        this.modifiers.addAll(modifiers)
+        return this
+    }
+
+    /** Supply the content (content-bearing views only). */
+    fun children(vararg children: View): ViewBuilder<V, C> {
+        this.children.addAll(children)
+        return this
+    }
+
+    override fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
+        if (children.isNotEmpty() && view is ChildrenView) {
+            view.setChildren(children)
+        }
+        var result: View = view
+        for (modifier in modifiers) {
+            result = Modified.apply(result, modifier)
+        }
+        return result.renderNode(env)
+    }
+}

+/** JNA binding to the Rust `libpathland_core` cdylib (SPSC ring + opcode engine). */
+class PathlandCore private constructor() {
+
+    /** Thrown when the native library cannot be linked. */
+    class NativeUnavailableException(message: String, cause: Throwable?) :
+        IllegalStateException(message, cause)
+
+    private interface NativePathlandCore : Library {
+        fun pathland_core_create(): Pointer
+        fun pathland_core_destroy(handle: Pointer)
+        fun pathland_ring_buffer_push(handle: Pointer, opcode: Pointer): Boolean
+        fun pathland_core_arena_alloc(handle: Pointer, bytes: Pointer, len: Int): Int
+        fun pathland_core_begin_frame(handle: Pointer)
+        fun pathland_core_end_frame(handle: Pointer)
+        fun pathland_core_frame_count(handle: Pointer): Int
+        fun pathland_core_ring_ptr(handle: Pointer): Pointer
+        fun pathland_core_ring_len(handle: Pointer): Long
+        fun pathland_core_ring_mut(handle: Pointer): Pointer
+        fun pathland_core_drain_events(handle: Pointer, out: Pointer, max: Int): Int
+        fun pathland_core_send_event(handle: Pointer, opcode: Pointer): Boolean
+    }
+
+    private val nativeCore: NativePathlandCore
+
+    /** Reused 16-byte opcode buffer (zero per-op heap allocations). */
+    private val opcodeBuf = Memory(Opcode.SIZE.toLong())
+
+    init {
+        try {
+            val libraryPath = resolveLibraryPath()
+                ?: throw NativeUnavailableException(
+                    "libpathland_core not found on java.library.path; " +
+                        "set the system property pathland.core.lib to its full path",
+                    null,
+                )
+            nativeCore = Native.load(libraryPath, NativePathlandCore::class.java)
+        } catch (e: NativeUnavailableException) {
+            throw e
+        } catch (t: Throwable) {
+            throw NativeUnavailableException("failed to link libpathland_core", t)
+        }
+    }
+
+    // --- ring host lifetime ---
+
+    /** Create a ring host over a fresh shared ring. */
+    fun create(): Pointer = nativeCore.pathland_core_create()
+
+    /** Destroy a ring host. */
+    fun destroy(handle: Pointer) {
+        nativeCore.pathland_core_destroy(handle)
+    }
+
+    // --- guest → host ring ---

+    /** Push one 16-byte opcode into the shared ring. Returns false when full. */
+    fun push(handle: Pointer, opcode: ByteArray): Boolean {
+        opcodeBuf.write(0, opcode, 0, Opcode.SIZE)
+        return nativeCore.pathland_ring_buffer_push(handle, opcodeBuf)
+    }
+
+    /** Allocate bytes into the bump arena, returning the absolute offset. */
+    fun arenaAlloc(handle: Pointer, bytes: ByteArray): Int {
+        val buf = Memory(maxOf(1, bytes.size).toLong())
+        if (bytes.isNotEmpty()) {
+            buf.write(0, bytes, 0, bytes.size)
+        }
+        return nativeCore.pathland_core_arena_alloc(handle, buf, bytes.size)
+    }
+
+    fun beginFrame(handle: Pointer) {
+        nativeCore.pathland_core_begin_frame(handle)
+    }
+
+    fun endFrame(handle: Pointer) {
+        nativeCore.pathland_core_end_frame(handle)
+    }
+
+    fun frameCount(handle: Pointer): Int = nativeCore.pathland_core_frame_count(handle)
+
+    /** Pointer to the shared linear memory (header | ring | arena). */
+    fun ringPtr(handle: Pointer): Pointer = nativeCore.pathland_core_ring_ptr(handle)
+
+    /** Byte length of the shared linear memory. */
+    fun ringLen(handle: Pointer): Long = nativeCore.pathland_core_ring_len(handle)
+
+    /** Borrow the underlying shared ring for a same-process consumer. */
+    fun ringMut(handle: Pointer): Pointer = nativeCore.pathland_core_ring_mut(handle)
+
+    // --- events (host → guest) ---
+
+    /** Drain pending EVENT opcodes into [out]; returns the number written. */
+    fun drainEvents(handle: Pointer, out: Pointer, max: Int): Int =
+        nativeCore.pathland_core_drain_events(handle, out, max)
+
+    /** Push one 16-byte EVENT opcode into the host → guest event ring. */
+    fun sendEvent(handle: Pointer, opcode: ByteArray): Boolean {
+        opcodeBuf.write(0, opcode, 0, Opcode.SIZE)
+        return nativeCore.pathland_core_send_event(handle, opcodeBuf)
+    }
+
+    companion object {
+        private object Holder {
+            val INSTANCE = PathlandCore()
+        }
+
+        /** The process-wide binding; lazily links `libpathland_core` on first call. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun instance(): PathlandCore = Holder.INSTANCE
+
+        /** Resolve the native library's full path. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun resolveLibraryPath(): String? {
+            val override = System.getProperty("pathland.core.lib")
+            if (override != null) return override
+            val fileName = "libpathland_core" + platformLibraryExtension()
+            val libraryPath = System.getProperty("java.library.path") ?: return null
+            for (dir in libraryPath.split(File.pathSeparator)) {
+                val candidate = File(dir, fileName)
+                if (candidate.isFile) return candidate.absolutePath
+            }
+            return null
+        }
+
+        private fun platformLibraryExtension(): String {
+            val os = System.getProperty("os.name", "").lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
+            if (os.contains("mac")) return ".dylib"
+            if (os.contains("win")) return ".dll"
+            return ".so"
+        }
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core.protocol
+
+/**
+ * A fixed-size 16-byte Pathland opcode (little-endian):
+ *
+ * `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32][B u32][C u32]`
+ *
+ * The component-named methods preserve the Java record accessor API
+ * (`op.category()`, `op.b()`, …) used by the renderers, hosts, and tests.
+ */
+data class Opcode(
+    val category: Int,
+    val command: Int,
+    val flags: Int,
+    val a: Int,
+    val b: Int,
+    val c: Int,
+) {
+    fun category(): Int = category
+    fun command(): Int = command
+    fun flags(): Int = flags
+    fun a(): Int = a
+    fun b(): Int = b
+    fun c(): Int = c
+
+    /** Serialize to the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
+    fun toBytes(): ByteArray {
+        val out = ByteArray(SIZE)
+        out[0] = category.toByte()
+        out[1] = command.toByte()
+        out[2] = flags.toByte()
+        out[3] = (flags ushr 8).toByte()
+        writeIntLE(out, 4, a)
+        writeIntLE(out, 8, b)
+        writeIntLE(out, 12, c)
+        return out
+    }
+
+    companion object {
+        const val SIZE = 16
+
+        /** Deserialize from the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun fromBytes(bytes: ByteArray): Opcode {
+            require(bytes.size == SIZE) { "opcode must be $SIZE bytes" }
+            return Opcode(
+                bytes[0].toInt() and 0xFF,
+                bytes[1].toInt() and 0xFF,
+                (bytes[2].toInt() and 0xFF) or ((bytes[3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8),
+                readIntLE(bytes, 4),
+                readIntLE(bytes, 8),
+                readIntLE(bytes, 12),
+            )
+        }
+
+        private fun writeIntLE(out: ByteArray, offset: Int, value: Int) {
+            out[offset] = value.toByte()
+            out[offset + 1] = (value ushr 8).toByte()
+            out[offset + 2] = (value ushr 16).toByte()
+            out[offset + 3] = (value ushr 24).toByte()
+        }
+
+        private fun readIntLE(bytes: ByteArray, offset: Int): Int =
+            (bytes[offset].toInt() and 0xFF) or
+                ((bytes[offset + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8) or
+                ((bytes[offset + 2].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 16) or
+                ((bytes[offset + 3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 24)
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core.protocol

+
+/** Encodes typed property values into their raw 32-bit wire payload. */
+object ValueEncoder {
+    /** Encode a typed value into its raw 32-bit wire payload for `SET_PROPERTY`. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun encodeBits(valueType: Int, value: Any): Int = when (valueType) {
+        ValueTypes.F32 -> (value as Float).toRawBits()
+        ValueTypes.COLOR -> (value as Color).argb()
+        ValueTypes.U8, ValueTypes.U32, ValueTypes.ENUM -> value as Int
+        else -> throw IllegalArgumentException("cannot encode value type $valueType")
+    }
+}

+    @JvmStatic
+    fun container(

+    ): ViewBuilder<NavigationContainer, NavigationContainer.Config> =
+        NavigationContainer.make { n -> n.router(router).chrome(chrome) }
+
+    /** A route list builder for a router seeded at `/`. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun navigator(): Builder = Builder("/")
+
+    /** A route list builder seeded at [initialPath]. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun navigator(initialPath: String): Builder = Builder(initialPath)
+
+    /** A reactive "is this the active route" signal. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun isActive(router: Router, path: String): Signal<Boolean> =
+        Signals.computed { router.path() == path }

+    /** A fluent route list → seeded Router builder. */
+    class Builder internal constructor(private val initialPath: String) {
+        private val table = RouteTable.builder()
+
+        fun route(pattern: String, view: View): Builder {
+            table.route(pattern, view)
+            return this
+        }
+
+        fun route(pattern: String, handler: RouteHandler): Builder {

+import dev.pathland.view.core.Configurable

+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Properties
+import dev.pathland.view.engine.PathlandNode
+import java.util.Objects
+import java.util.function.Consumer
+
+/** The navigation slot: a structural container whose single child is the current route. */
+class NavigationContainer private constructor(
+    private val config: Config,
+) : View, Configurable<NavigationContainer.Config> {
+
+    /** NavigationContainer values. */
+    class Config : View.Config {
+        var router: Router? = null
+        var chrome: Chrome = Chrome.PLATFORM_DEFAULT
+
+        fun router(router: Router): Config {
+            this.router = router
+            return this
+        }
+
+        fun chrome(chrome: Chrome): Config {
+            this.chrome = chrome
+            return this
+        }
+    }
+
+    override fun config(): Config = config
+
+    override fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
+        val router = Objects.requireNonNull(config.router, "router")!!
+        val chrome = Objects.requireNonNull(config.chrome, "chrome")
+        val node = PathlandNode(Components.VSTACK)
+        val scope = Environment.current().with(Navigation.ROUTER, router)
+        val previous = Environment.current()
+        Environment.within(scope)
+        try {
+            val selected = router.destination()
+            if (selected != null) {
+                node.children.add(selected.render(env))
+            }
+        } finally {
+            Environment.restore(previous)
+        }
+        node.properties[Properties.ROUTE] = router.path()
+        node.properties[Properties.NAV_DEPTH] = router.depth()
+        node.properties[Properties.NAV_CHROME] = chrome.wire().toFloat()
+        node.properties[Properties.TRANSITION] = 1f
+        node.navigateHandler = Consumer { event -> router.handleEvent(event) }
+        node.router = router
+        return node
+    }
+
+    companion object {
+        /** An empty NavigationContainer (no values). */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun make(): ViewBuilder<NavigationContainer, Config> =
+            ViewBuilder(NavigationContainer(Config()))
+
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun make(configure: Consumer<Config>): ViewBuilder<NavigationContainer, Config> {
+            val config = Config()
+            configure.accept(config)
+            return ViewBuilder(NavigationContainer(config))
+        }
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core.router
+
+import java.util.Collections
+import java.util.Objects
+
+/** Path parameters captured from a route pattern, plus the matched path. */
+class Params private constructor(
+    private val values: Map<String, String>,
+    private val matchedPath: String?,
+) {
+    fun path(): String? = matchedPath
+
+    /** The raw string value of a param, or null when absent. */
+    operator fun get(name: String): String? = values[name]
+
+    fun intValue(name: String): Int = try {
+        get(name)!!.toInt()
+    } catch (_: RuntimeException) {
+        0
+    }
+
+    fun longValue(name: String): Long = try {
+        get(name)!!.toLong()
+    } catch (_: RuntimeException) {
+        0L
+    }
+
+    fun doubleValue(name: String): Double = try {
+        get(name)!!.toDouble()
+    } catch (_: RuntimeException) {
+        0.0
+    }
+
+    fun booleanValue(name: String): Boolean {
+        val v = get(name)
+        return v != null && (v.equals("true", ignoreCase = true) || v == "1")
+    }
+
+    fun contains(name: String): Boolean = values.containsKey(name)
+    fun isEmpty(): Boolean = values.isEmpty()
+
+    override fun equals(other: Any?): Boolean =
+        other is Params && values == other.values && matchedPath == other.matchedPath
+
+    override fun hashCode(): Int = Objects.hash(values, matchedPath)
+    override fun toString(): String = "Params$values"
+
+    companion object {
+        private val NONE = Params(emptyMap(), null)
+
+        /** An empty param set. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun none(): Params = NONE
+
+        /** Wrap captured path params plus the matched path. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun of(values: Map<String, String>, path: String?): Params =
+            Params(Collections.unmodifiableMap(values), path)
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core.router
+
+import java.util.Objects
+
+/** A navigation route: the absolute path that identifies a destination. */
+data class Route(val path: String) {
+    init {
+        Objects.requireNonNull(path, "path")
+        require(path.startsWith("/")) { "route paths must be absolute: $path" }
+    }
+
+    fun path(): String = path
+
+    /** The path with any query/fragment stripped. */
+    fun pathOnly(): String = pathOnly(path)
+
+    companion object {
+        /** A route for an absolute path. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun of(path: String): Route = Route(path)
+
+        private fun pathOnly(path: String): String {
+            var end = path.length
+            val query = path.indexOf('?')
+            val fragment = path.indexOf('#')
+            if (query >= 0) end = minOf(end, query)
+            if (fragment >= 0) end = minOf(end, fragment)
+            return path.substring(0, end)
+        }
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core.signal
+
+import java.util.ArrayDeque
+
+/** The reactive evaluation context: a thread-local stack of consumers. */
+internal object ReactiveContext {
+    private val STACK: ThreadLocal<ArrayDeque<ReactiveNode>> =
+        ThreadLocal.withInitial { ArrayDeque() }
+
+    /** The consumer currently evaluating, or null outside any reactive context. */
+    fun current(): ReactiveNode? = STACK.get().peek()
+
+    /** The underlying stack (used by `Signals.untracked`). */
+    fun stack(): ArrayDeque<ReactiveNode> = STACK.get()
+
+    /** Whether [node] is currently being evaluated (reentrancy guard). */
+    fun contains(node: ReactiveNode): Boolean = STACK.get().contains(node)
+
+    fun push(node: ReactiveNode) {
+        val stack = STACK.get()
+        if (stack.contains(node)) {
+            throw IllegalStateException(
+                "Circular signal dependency detected while evaluating '${node.describe()}'",
+            )
+        }
+        stack.push(node)
+    }
+
+    fun pop() {
+        STACK.get().pop()
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core.signal
+
+import java.util.ArrayDeque
+import java.util.Objects
+import java.util.function.BiPredicate
+import java.util.function.Consumer
+import java.util.function.Supplier
+
+/** Factory for Angular-style reactive primitives. */
+object Signals {
+
+    /** A writable signal with `Objects.equals` equality. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun <T> signal(initial: T): WritableSignal<T> =
+        WritableSignalImpl(initial, Objects::equals, null)
+
+    /** A writable signal with a custom equality comparator. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun <T> signal(initial: T, equal: BiPredicate<T, T>): WritableSignal<T> =
+        WritableSignalImpl(initial, Objects.requireNonNull(equal, "equal"), null)
+
+    /** A named writable signal. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun <T> signal(name: String, initial: T): WritableSignal<T> =
+        WritableSignalImpl(initial, Objects::equals, name)
+
+    /** An immutable signal carrying a static value. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun <T> constant(value: T): Signal<T> = ConstantSignal(value)
+
+    /** A lazy, memoized derived signal. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun <T> computed(fn: Supplier<T>): Signal<T> =
+        ComputedSignal(Objects.requireNonNull(fn, "computed body"), Objects::equals)
+
+    /** A derived signal with a custom equality comparator. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun <T> computed(fn: Supplier<T>, equal: BiPredicate<T, T>): Signal<T> =
+        ComputedSignal(
+            Objects.requireNonNull(fn, "computed body"),
+            Objects.requireNonNull(equal, "equal"),
+        )
+
+    /** Register an effect; runs immediately, then on tracked dependency changes. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun effect(fn: Runnable): EffectRef = effect(fn, EffectOptions.DEFAULT)
+
+    /** Register an effect with options. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun effect(fn: Runnable, options: EffectOptions): EffectRef =
+        Effect(Objects.requireNonNull(fn, "effect body"), Objects.requireNonNull(options, "options"), null)
+
+    /** A named effect. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun effect(name: String, fn: Runnable): EffectRef =
+        Effect(Objects.requireNonNull(fn, "effect body"), EffectOptions.DEFAULT, name)
+
+    /** A synchronous tracked computation (emitter-internal). */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun <T> tracked(fn: Supplier<T>, onRecompute: Consumer<T>): Tracked<T> {
+        Objects.requireNonNull(fn, "tracked body")
+        Objects.requireNonNull(onRecompute, "tracked recompute")
+        val computed = ComputedSignal(fn, Objects::equals)
+        val initial = untracked(Supplier { computed.get() })
+        var first = true
+        val effect = effect(Runnable {
+            val value = computed.get()
+            if (first) {
+                first = false
+                if (!Objects.equals(value, initial)) {
+                    onRecompute.accept(value)
+                }
+                return@Runnable
+            }
+            onRecompute.accept(value)
+        })
+        return Tracked(initial, effect)
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Read signals without recording dependencies on the enclosing context.
+     */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun <T> untracked(fn: Supplier<T>): T {
+        val stack = ReactiveContext.stack()
+        val saved = ArrayDeque(stack)
+        stack.clear()
+        try {
+            return Objects.requireNonNull(fn, "untracked body").get()
+        } finally {
+            stack.addAll(saved)
+        }
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core.signal
+
+import java.util.function.BiPredicate
+import java.util.function.UnaryOperator
+
+/** A writable signal backed by a reactive graph node. */
+internal class WritableSignalImpl<T>(
+    private var value: T,
+    private val equal: BiPredicate<T, T>,
+    name: String?,
+) : ReactiveNode(name), WritableSignal<T> {
+
+    override fun get(): T {
+        recordDependency()
+        return value
+    }
+
+    override fun set(value: T) {
+        if (equal.test(this.value, value)) return
+        checkWriteAllowed()
+        this.value = value
+        version++
+        propagate()
+    }
+
+    override fun update(fn: UnaryOperator<T>) {
+        set(fn.apply(value))
+    }
+
+    override fun asReadonly(): Signal<T> = Signal { get() }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core.state
+
+import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.EffectRef
+import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signals
+import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.WritableSignal
+
+/**
+ * Per-session persisted state. [signal] creates a signal that auto-loads its
+ * persisted value and auto-saves on change, keyed `"name:scope"`; signals are
+ * memoized by name.
+ */
+class PersistentState(
+    private val store: StateStore,
+    private val scope: String?,
+) : AutoCloseable {
+
+    private val signals = HashMap<String, WritableSignal<*>>()
+    private val persistEffects = ArrayList<EffectRef>()
+
+    /** Create (or return) the signal named [name], auto-loading and auto-saving it. */
+    @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
+    fun <T : Any> signal(name: String, initial: T): WritableSignal<T> {
+        val existing = signals[name] as WritableSignal<T>?
+        if (existing != null) return existing
+
+        val key = scoped(name)
+        val signal = Signals.signal(name, store.load(key, initial.javaClass).orElse(initial))
+        signals[name] = signal
+        persistEffects.add(Signals.effect {
+            try {
+                store.save(key, signal.get())
+            } catch (_: RuntimeException) {
+                // Persistence is best-effort for a UI component.
+            }
+        })
+        return signal
+    }
+
+    private fun scoped(name: String): String =
+        if (scope.isNullOrEmpty()) name else "$name:$scope"
+
+    override fun close() {
+        for (effect in persistEffects) {
+            effect.destroy()
+        }
+        persistEffects.clear()
+        signals.clear()
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core.state
+
+import java.util.Optional
+
+/**
+ * A cross-platform state store abstraction. The same application code runs on a
+ * multi-tenant server (Redis), a desktop app (File/SQLite), a browser
+ * (LocalStorage), or an embedded target by swapping the implementation.
+ */
+interface StateStore {
+    /** Load state for [key] (type-checked against [clazz]), or empty when absent. */
+    fun <T : Any> load(key: String, clazz: Class<T>): Optional<T>
+
+    /** Persist [state] for [key]. */
+    fun save(key: String, state: Any)
+
+    /** Remove state for [key]. */
+    fun delete(key: String)
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core.transport
+
+/**
+ * The platform's environment data: viewport size and the initial route, delivered
+ * as `META::ENVIRONMENT` fields.
+ */
+class EnvironmentData(
+    route: String?,
+    val viewportWidth: Float,
+    val viewportHeight: Float,
+) {
+    val route: String = normalize(route)
+
+    fun route(): String = route
+    fun viewportWidth(): Float = viewportWidth
+    fun viewportHeight(): Float = viewportHeight
+
+    companion object {
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun of(route: String?): EnvironmentData = EnvironmentData(route, -1f, -1f)
+
+        private fun normalize(route: String?): String {
+            var normalized = if (route.isNullOrBlank()) "/" else route
+            if (!normalized.startsWith("/")) normalized = "/$normalized"
+            return normalized
+        }
+    }
+}

+package dev.pathland.view.core.transport

+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Categories
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Commands
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Opcode
+import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream
+import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
+
+/** The network batch codec — mirrors `pathland_core_transport`. */
+object FrameCodec {
+    const val MAGIC = 0x504C_504C
+    const val VERSION = 1
+    const val GUEST_TO_HOST = 0x0000
+    const val HOST_TO_GUEST = 0x0001
+    const val HEADER = 16
+
+    /** Encode a self-contained frame as a network batch (sequence 0). */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun encodeFrame(frame: ProtocolFrame): ByteArray = encodeFrame(frame, 0)
+
+    /** Encode a self-contained frame as a guest → host batch with [sequence]. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun encodeFrame(frame: ProtocolFrame, sequence: Int): ByteArray {
+        val out = ByteArrayOutputStream()
+        writeHeader(out, GUEST_TO_HOST, sequence, frame.opcodes.size)
+        for (op in frame.opcodes) {
+            writeBytes(out, op.toBytes())
+        }
+        writeIntLE(out, frame.strings.size)
+        writeBytes(out, frame.strings)
+        return out.toByteArray()
+    }
+
+    /** Decode a self-contained frame batch into opcodes + string section. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun decodeFrame(bytes: ByteArray): ProtocolFrame {
+        val parsed = parse(bytes)
+        return ProtocolFrame(parsed.opcodes, parsed.strings)
+    }
+
+    /** The per-stream message sequence encoded in a batch header (offset 8). */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun sequence(bytes: ByteArray): Int {
+        if (bytes.size < HEADER) throw IllegalArgumentException("batch truncated")
+        return readIntLE(bytes, 8)
+    }
+
+    /** Encode a `META::RESYNC` request batch (host → guest). */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun encodeResync(): ByteArray = singleMeta(Commands.Meta.RESYNC)
+
+    /** Encode a `META::PONG` reply batch (host → guest). */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun encodePong(): ByteArray = singleMeta(Commands.Meta.PONG)
+
+    /** Encode a `META::PING` heartbeat probe batch (guest → host). */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun encodePing(): ByteArray {
+        val out = ByteArrayOutputStream()
+        writeHeader(out, GUEST_TO_HOST, 0, 1)
+        writeBytes(out, Opcode(Categories.META, Commands.Meta.PING, 0, 0, 0, 0).toBytes())
+        writeIntLE(out, 0)
+        return out.toByteArray()
+    }

+    private fun singleMeta(command: Int): ByteArray {
+        val out = ByteArrayOutputStream()
+        writeHeader(out, HOST_TO_GUEST, 0, 1)
+        writeBytes(out, Opcode(Categories.META, command, 0, 0, 0, 0).toBytes())
+        writeIntLE(out, 0)
+        return out.toByteArray()
+    }

+    /** Encode a `META::ENVIRONMENT` field batch (viewport + route). */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun encodeEnvironment(env: EnvironmentData): ByteArray {
+        val route = env.route.toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
+        val ops = ArrayList<Opcode>(3)
+        if (env.viewportWidth > 0) {
+            ops.add(Opcode(Categories.META, Commands.Meta.ENVIRONMENT, 0,
+                Commands.Environment.VIEWPORT_WIDTH, env.viewportWidth.toRawBits(), 0))
+        }
+        if (env.viewportHeight > 0) {
+            ops.add(Opcode(Categories.META, Commands.Meta.ENVIRONMENT, 0,
+                Commands.Environment.VIEWPORT_HEIGHT, env.viewportHeight.toRawBits(), 0))
+        }
+        ops.add(Opcode(Categories.META, Commands.Meta.ENVIRONMENT, 0,
+            Commands.Environment.ROUTE, 0, 0))
+        val out = ByteArrayOutputStream()
+        writeHeader(out, HOST_TO_GUEST, 0, ops.size)
+        for (op in ops) {
+            writeBytes(out, op.toBytes())
+        }
+        writeIntLE(out, 4 + route.size)
+        writeIntLE(out, route.size)
+        out.writeBytes(route)
+        return out.toByteArray()
+    }

+    @JvmStatic

+        parse(bytes).opcodes.any { it.category == Categories.META && it.command == Commands.Meta.RESYNC }
+
+    /** True when the batch carries a `META::PING` heartbeat probe. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun isPing(bytes: ByteArray): Boolean =
+        parse(bytes).opcodes.any { it.category == Categories.META && it.command == Commands.Meta.PING }

+                Commands.Environment.VIEWPORT_WIDTH -> width = Float.fromBits(op.b)
+                Commands.Environment.VIEWPORT_HEIGHT -> height = Float.fromBits(op.b)
+                Commands.Environment.ROUTE -> route = parsed.stringAt(op.b)

+    }

+    /** Encode host → guest events as a batch. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun encodeEvents(events: List<Event>): ByteArray {

+            when {
+                event.isTextChanged -> {

+                    val utf8 = event.text.orEmpty().toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)

+                    strings.writeBytes(utf8)

+                    Categories.EVENT, Commands.Event.VALUE_CHANGED, 0,
+                    event.target, event.value.toRawBits(), 0))

+                event.isDateChanged -> opcodes.add(Opcode(

+        writeHeader(out, HOST_TO_GUEST, 0, opcodes.size)
+        for (op in opcodes) {
+            writeBytes(out, op.toBytes())
+        }
+        writeIntLE(out, strings.size())
+        writeBytes(out, strings.toByteArray())
+        return out.toByteArray()
+    }
+
+    /** Decode a host → guest event batch into typed events. */
+    @JvmStatic
+    fun decodeEvents(bytes: ByteArray): List<Event> {
+        val parsed = parse(bytes)
+        val events = ArrayList<Event>()
+        for (op in parsed.opcodes) {
+            if (op.category != Categories.EVENT) continue
+            when (op.command) {
+                Commands.Event.TEXT_CHANGED -> events.add(Event.textChanged(op.a, parsed.stringAt(op.b)))
+                Commands.Event.NAVIGATE -> events.add(
+                    if ((op.flags and Commands.Flags.NAVIGATE_URL) != 0) {
+                        Event.navigate(parsed.stringAt(op.b))
+                    } else {
+                        Event.navigateBack()
+                    })
+                Commands.Event.VALUE_CHANGED -> events.add(Event.valueChanged(op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b)))
+                Commands.Event.KEY_DOWN -> events.add(Event.keyDown(op.a, op.b, op.c, op.flags))
+                Commands.Event.KEY_UP -> events.add(Event.keyUp(op.a, op.b, op.c))
+                Commands.Event.DATE_CHANGED -> events.add(Event.dateChanged(op.a, op.b, op.c))
+                Commands.Event.FOCUS_CHANGED -> events.add(Event.focusChanged(op.a, op.b != 0))
+                Commands.Event.EDITING_CHANGED -> events.add(Event.editingChanged(op.a, op.b != 0))
+                Commands.Event.SUBMIT -> events.add(Event.submit(op.a))
+                Commands.Event.SCROLL -> events.add(Event.scroll(
+                    op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b), Float.fromBits(op.c)))
+                Commands.Event.WHEEL -> events.add(Event.wheel(
+                    op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b), Float.fromBits(op.c)))
+                Commands.Event.MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED -> events.add(
+                    Event.mediaPlayStateChanged(op.a, op.b != 0))
+                Commands.Event.MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED -> events.add(
+                    Event.mediaTimeUpdated(op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b)))
+                Commands.Event.MEDIA_ENDED -> events.add(Event.mediaEnded(op.a))
+                Commands.Event.MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED -> events.add(
+                    Event.mediaVolumeChanged(op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b)))
+                Commands.Event.MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED -> events.add(
+                    Event.mediaDurationChanged(op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b)))
+                Commands.Event.FIT_CHANGED -> events.add(
+                    Event.fitChanged(op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b)))
+                Commands.Event.POINTER_DOWN, Commands.Event.POINTER_MOVE, Commands.Event.POINTER_UP ->
+                    events.add(Event(op.command, op.a, op.flags, Float.fromBits(op.b),
